common_meaning: A swirling pattern in the polarisation of the cosmic microwave background, the oldest light in the universe.
example: Telescopes at the South Pole search for primordial B-mode polarization.
rrgm_bridge: A pattern with more than one possible source. Detecting the pattern and identifying its source are separate steps.
invariant_mi: The curl-type component of the polarisation pattern of the cosmic microwave background.

domain_entries.PHY: Produced by gravitational lensing of the other polarisation component, by galactic dust, and possibly by gravitational waves from the very early universe.

count_condition: A polarisation map decomposed into its curl-type and gradient-type parts.
transfer_boundary: Detecting B-modes is not detecting primordial gravitational waves; a 2014 claim turned out to be dust. Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

common_meaning: To talk rapidly and continuously in a foolish or confused way; the speech-like sounds of an infant; a murmuring sound.
example: The baby babbled happily in her cot.
rrgm_bridge: Speech-like form without recoverable content. In infants it is practice of the form before the content arrives.
invariant_mi: Continuous speech-like sound without recoverable meaning.

domain_entries.LIN: A stage of infant development in which syllables are repeated before words appear.
domain_entries.COG: The noise of many voices at once, used to test hearing in realistic conditions.
domain_entries.DIG: Fluent output that carries no usable content.

count_condition: A stream of speech-like sound, and no meaning recoverable by a competent hearer.
transfer_boundary: Infant babbling is structured practice and not mere noise. Fluent is not meaningful. Not "Babel".

common_meaning: A very young child or animal; the youngest of a group; to treat someone as a baby.
example: The baby slept through the night.
rrgm_bridge: Full standing with no capacity yet for self-rule. Care for a baby is the clearest case of responsibility resting on one side.
invariant_mi: A human or animal in the earliest stage after birth, dependent on care.

domain_entries.BIO: The newborn and infant stage, marked by rapid growth and dependence.
domain_entries.REL: A dependant owed care; also a term of endearment or of belittlement.
domain_entries.COG: The period of earliest perceptual and social learning.
domain_entries.LIN: "Baby talk": the simplified, high-pitched register adults use with infants.
domain_entries.PEJ: "Don't be a baby" and "crybaby" shame an adult's distress by casting it as infantile. Provisional domain.

count_condition: An individual in the earliest post-birth stage of its species.
transfer_boundary: A baby is not a foetus and not a toddler. To baby a capable person is to take decisions from them.

common_meaning: The rear surface of the human body from shoulders to hips; the side or part furthest from the front.
example: He carried the child on his back.
rrgm_bridge: The side away from the direction of facing. It depends on which way the thing is taken to face.
invariant_mi: The rear side or part of something, opposite its front.

domain_entries.BIO: The dorsal surface of the trunk, supported by the spine.
domain_entries.PHY: The rear part of an object or space.

count_condition: An object with an identified front, and the side opposite it.
transfer_boundary: Front and back are assigned by orientation or use and are not fixed properties of every object.

common_meaning: In or to an earlier place, position, or condition; in return.
example: She went back to the house for her keys.
rrgm_bridge: Marks return. As with "again", it can mean to a place or state as it was, or to the same function with something changed.
invariant_mi: Toward or at an earlier place, state, or party, in return.

domain_entries.LIN: An adverb of return (go back), restoration (put it back), and reciprocity (write back).
domain_entries.DIG: Navigation to a prior state; a response returned to a caller.

count_condition: An earlier place, state, or sender, and motion or response directed to it.
transfer_boundary: Going back to a place is not undoing what happened since. Giving back is not paying back.

common_meaning: To give support to; to bet on; to provide security for.
example: The union backed the proposal.
rrgm_bridge: Stands behind something so that it does not fall, usually by committing one's own resources or name.
invariant_mi: To stand behind something with support that it can rely on.

domain_entries.REL: To endorse or support a person or cause.
domain_entries.ECO: To finance; to secure a currency or loan with assets.

count_condition: A supporter, a thing supported, and committed support.
transfer_boundary: Backing is not agreeing with everything backed. A backed claim is not thereby true.

common_meaning: A reference to something that appeared earlier in the same text or structure.
example: The pronoun "it" is a back-reference to "the report".
rrgm_bridge: Takes its value from an earlier item. If the earlier item is no longer reachable, the reference dangles and should be reported as missing.
invariant_mi: A reference that points to an earlier item in the same text or structure and takes its value from it.

domain_entries.LIN: Anaphora: a pronoun or phrase interpreted through an earlier expression.
domain_entries.DIG: In a pattern, a marker that must match the same text as an earlier group; in compression, a pointer to an earlier occurrence; in dialogue, a pointer to an earlier turn.

count_condition: An earlier item, a later pointer, and a rule by which the pointer resolves to the item.
transfer_boundary: A back-reference is not a citation of an outside source. It fails when the earlier item has passed out of reach.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The spine; the chief support of a system or organisation; strength of character.
example: Small farms are the backbone of the region.
rrgm_bridge: The central line that bears load and to which the rest attaches. The specific character usually lies in what attaches.
invariant_mi: The central load-bearing line of a structure, to which other parts attach.

domain_entries.BIO: The vertebral column; the repeating chain of a protein or nucleic acid, as distinct from its side groups.
domain_entries.DIG: The high-capacity core links of a network; the base network of a model to which task-specific parts are added.
domain_entries.REL: The members or part on which an organisation depends; firmness of character.

count_condition: A structure, a central supporting line, and parts attached to it.
transfer_boundary: The backbone is not the whole. Courage called "backbone" is figurative.

common_meaning: The part of a scene behind the main objects; the circumstances behind an event; a person's origins and experience; out of notice.
example: The mountains form the background of the painting.
rrgm_bridge: What the attended thing stands out against and is understood by. Change the background and the same figure reads differently.
invariant_mi: What lies behind or before the thing attended to, against which it stands out and by which it is understood.

domain_entries.COG: The ground in perception, as opposed to the figure.
domain_entries.PHY: Signal not from the source of interest, which must be measured and subtracted.
domain_entries.DIG: Processes that run without user interaction.
domain_entries.REL: A person's social, educational, and work history.
domain_entries.LIN: Information treated as given or presupposed in discourse.

count_condition: A focus, and a surrounding field or prior context against which it is taken.
transfer_boundary: Background is not irrelevant. What counts as background depends on what is attended and can switch.

common_meaning: A standing condition that must hold for something to happen or apply, but that is taken for granted and not named as its cause.
example: Oxygen is a background-condition for the match lighting.
rrgm_bridge: Presupposed and unnamed. When one changes silently, results fail with no visible reason.
invariant_mi: A standing condition that must hold for something to occur or apply, presupposed and not named as its cause.

domain_entries.COG: In causal reasoning, an enabling condition as distinct from the cause picked out.
domain_entries.PHY: Ambient and boundary conditions of an experiment.
domain_entries.DIG: The environment, configuration, and deployment context that an output depends on.
domain_entries.REL: Conditions such as freedom from coercion that make consent or agreement valid.

count_condition: An event or claim, a condition without which it fails, and that condition's being presupposed.
transfer_boundary: Which factor is called "the cause" and which a background condition depends on the question asked. A condition is a state of the world; an assumption is a belief about it.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The division of what is perceived or presented into what is in focus and what lies behind it.
example: The optical illusion works by reversing background-foreground.
rrgm_bridge: A division made by attention. Reversing it changes what is seen while nothing in the field changes.
invariant_mi: The division of a field into what is attended as figure and what recedes as ground, and the relation between the two.

domain_entries.COG: Figure and ground organisation in perception, including reversible figures.
domain_entries.LIN: Foregrounding and backgrounding of information in discourse and style.
domain_entries.DIG: Separation of subject from surroundings in images; processes that hold the user's focus versus those that do not.

count_condition: A field, a part taken as focus, and the remainder taken as ground.
transfer_boundary: Foreground is not "important" and background "unimportant". The division is not a property of the things divided.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. QA: source ID F242 is filed under F while the headword sorts under B; ID kept unchanged.

common_meaning: What a person already knows and brings, unstated, to understanding something new.
example: The joke only works if the audience has the right background-knowledge.
rrgm_bridge: The standing store that interpretation draws on. In a digital system the trained store is fixed, and what is supplied in context is a separate route.
invariant_mi: What a party already knows and brings, unstated, to understanding something new.

domain_entries.COG: Prior knowledge that shapes comprehension and inference.
domain_entries.LIN: The common ground a speaker presumes the hearer shares.
domain_entries.FOR: The information on which a probability or inference is conditioned.
domain_entries.DIG: What a system holds from training, as distinct from what it is given in context.

count_condition: A party, something new to be understood, and prior knowledge brought to it.
transfer_boundary: Background knowledge may be wrong or out of date. What a speaker presumes shared may not be shared.
remainder_note: An established term, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A copy of data kept in case the original is lost; a reserve or support.
example: Make a backup before you update the system.
rrgm_bridge: A second kept ready to stand in for a first. Restoring from it returns to the earlier state and loses what came after.
invariant_mi: A second thing kept ready to take the place of a first if it fails.

domain_entries.DIG: A stored copy from which data can be restored.
domain_entries.REL: Reserve personnel or a fallback plan.

count_condition: A primary, a reserve, and a condition under which the reserve is used.
transfer_boundary: A backup is not an archive, a mirror, or live redundancy. An untested backup is a hope.
remainder_note: Not entered: backup as a build-up behind a blockage.

common_meaning: A virus that infects bacteria.
example: The bacteriophage injects its DNA into the cell.
rrgm_bridge: A replicator that can only run inside a host of the right kind.
invariant_mi: A virus whose host is a bacterium.

domain_entries.BIO: Either bursts the cell after replicating or lies dormant in the host genome; used in research and in treating some infections.

count_condition: A virus shown to infect and replicate in bacteria.
transfer_boundary: Bacteriophages do not infect human cells. Not an antibiotic. Often shortened to "phage".

common_meaning: Of poor quality; unpleasant; morally wrong; harmful; not valid.
example: The milk has gone bad.
rrgm_bridge: A verdict that needs its standard: bad at what, for whom, by which measure. A bad output is not thereby a bad producer.
invariant_mi: Falling short of what the relevant standard requires or desires.

domain_entries.LIN: The general negative evaluative, with irregular comparison (worse, worst).
domain_entries.REL: Morally wrong or blameworthy.
domain_entries.DIG: Invalid or malformed, as with a bad request or bad sector.
domain_entries.ECO: Uncollectable (bad debt).

count_condition: A thing, a standard, and a shortfall against it.
transfer_boundary: Bad is not evil, incorrect, or harmful by default; each needs its own showing. Unqualified, the word is a verdict without its measure.

common_meaning: The quality of being bad.
example: The badness of the plan was plain to everyone but its author.
rrgm_bridge: The degree or fact of falling short, on one named dimension.
invariant_mi: The degree or fact of falling short of a standard, or of having negative value.

domain_entries.COG: In the theory of value, what makes a state of affairs worse.
domain_entries.REL: Moral wrongness.
domain_entries.DIG: A numeric penalty scoring how poor a candidate solution is.

count_condition: A thing, a dimension, and a measure or judgement of shortfall.
transfer_boundary: Badness of an outcome is not blameworthiness of an agent.

common_meaning: A flexible container with an opening at the top; in mathematics and computing, a collection that allows duplicates and ignores order.
example: She packed a bag for the weekend.
rrgm_bridge: Holds things together without arranging them: membership and count are kept, and order is dropped.
invariant_mi: A flexible container that holds things loosely together without arranging them.

domain_entries.PHY: A container that takes the shape of its contents.
domain_entries.FOR: A multiset: an unordered collection in which items can repeat.
domain_entries.DIG: A text representation that keeps word counts and discards word order.
domain_entries.LIN: Idioms such as "mixed bag" and "in the bag".

count_condition: A container or collection, contents, and no fixed arrangement among them.
transfer_boundary: A bag is not a set (no repeats) and not a list (ordered).

common_meaning: To cook by dry heat in an oven; to harden by heat; in computing, to compute something in advance and fix it in.
example: Bake the bread for forty minutes.
rrgm_bridge: An irreversible fixing. What is baked in cannot be stirred back out.
invariant_mi: To fix something into a lasting form by sustained dry heat, or by analogy to compute it ahead and fix it in.

domain_entries.PHY: Heat-driven changes that set dough or fire clay.
domain_entries.DIG: Precomputing results into stored data; building settings into an image or model so that they cannot be changed at run time.
domain_entries.LIN: "Half-baked": not thought through.

count_condition: A prior workable state, a fixing process, and a resulting form that cannot be returned to the prior state.
transfer_boundary: Baking is not boiling or drying. Baked-in is the opposite of configurable.

common_meaning: A place where bread and cakes are made or sold.
example: The bakery opens at six.
rrgm_bridge: A place of production named for its process.
invariant_mi: An establishment that produces baked goods, sells them, or both.

domain_entries.ECO: A food business, from craft shop to industrial plant.

count_condition: Premises where baked goods are made or sold as the main activity.
transfer_boundary: A shop that only reheats bought-in dough is a bakery in name more than in process.

common_meaning: An even distribution of weight that keeps something steady; a state in which opposing forces or influences are equal or in proportion.
example: She lost her balance on the ice.
rrgm_bridge: Opposed weights or claims in a relation where neither overturns the other. It is usually held by continual small correction.
invariant_mi: A condition in which opposed weights, forces, or claims offset one another.

domain_entries.PHY: Equilibrium of forces and moments.
domain_entries.BIO: The sense and control of bodily posture; steady states such as fluid balance.
domain_entries.REL: Due proportion among competing interests or powers.

count_condition: Two or more opposed weights or influences, and their mutual offsetting.
transfer_boundary: Balance is not stillness: much balance is dynamic. Not equality: due proportion may be unequal.
remainder_note: Source IDs B040, B052, B211, B301. Which sense each legacy ID carried was not consulted; all are kept on each sense record. The Balance Floor preprint uses "balance floor" for the fixed set of a reflection in its treatment of the critical line; that technical use is not entered here.

common_meaning: An instrument for weighing; to weigh one thing against another.
example: The chemist placed the sample on the balance.
rrgm_bridge: Comparison by setting two things against each other on one instrument.
invariant_mi: An instrument or act that compares two weights or considerations by setting them against each other.

domain_entries.PHY: A weighing device comparing an unknown mass with a known one.
domain_entries.COG: Weighing considerations in reaching a judgement.

count_condition: Two things compared and a common measure on which they are set against each other.
transfer_boundary: A balance compares masses and reads the same wherever gravity is uniform across it, unlike a spring scale.

common_meaning: The amount of money in an account; an amount still owed; what is left over.
example: The balance is due on delivery.
rrgm_bridge: The net of everything written so far. It shows where things stand and hides the path.
invariant_mi: The net amount remaining after credits and debits, or what remains of a whole.

domain_entries.ECO: The difference between the two sides of an account; a sum outstanding.
domain_entries.FOR: The remainder after a subtraction.

count_condition: A record of additions and subtractions, and their net.
transfer_boundary: A balance is a net figure at a time. Equal balances can come from different histories.

common_meaning: In a state of balance; taking all sides fairly into account; arranged in good proportion.
example: The report gives a balanced view of the evidence.
rrgm_bridge: Reports that the proportions are right for the purpose. In an account of evidence, the right proportion follows the evidence and need not be equal.
invariant_mi: Having opposing parts or weights in equal or due proportion.

domain_entries.PHY: Of forces: summing to zero. Of a chemical equation: with the same atoms on both sides.
domain_entries.FOR: Of a tree or bracket sequence: meeting a defined symmetry condition.
domain_entries.DIG: Of load or data classes: spread evenly.
domain_entries.ECO: Of a budget: with spending matched by revenue.
domain_entries.LIN: Of an account: giving each side its due weight.

count_condition: Opposed parts, a standard of proportion, and conformity to it.
transfer_boundary: Balanced is not neutral. Giving equal weight to unequal evidence is false balance.

common_meaning: The act of bringing things into balance or keeping them there.
example: Balancing work and family took constant effort.
rrgm_bridge: The ongoing adjustment, where "balance" names the state reached.
invariant_mi: The continuing act of adjusting opposed weights or claims so that neither overwhelms.

domain_entries.REL: In law, a test that weighs competing interests case by case.
domain_entries.DIG: Distributing requests across servers.
domain_entries.ECO: Reconciling accounts; matching supply to demand on a grid.
domain_entries.BIO: Selection that keeps more than one variant in a population.

count_condition: Opposed weights or claims and repeated adjustment between them.
transfer_boundary: Balancing is not splitting the difference. Some claims are held to be outside balancing altogether.

common_meaning: A platform projecting from the wall of a building, with a railing; the upstairs seats in a theatre.
example: They had breakfast on the balcony.
rrgm_bridge: Part of the inside that stands outside. One can see and be seen from it without leaving.
invariant_mi: A railed platform projecting from an upper wall of a building.

domain_entries.PHY: A cantilevered or supported platform open to the air.
domain_entries.REL: An upper seating tier in a theatre; a place from which crowds are addressed.

count_condition: A building, an upper-level projecting platform, and a guard rail.
transfer_boundary: A balcony is not a terrace (on the ground or a roof) or a veranda (roofed, at ground level).

common_meaning: A solid or hollow sphere, especially one used in games; a rounded mass or part.
example: The dog chased the ball.
rrgm_bridge: A body with no preferred direction. In games it also marks whose turn it is.
invariant_mi: A solid or hollow round body, or a rounded mass.

domain_entries.PHY: A sphere or near-sphere, rolling and bouncing predictably.
domain_entries.FOR: The set of all points within a given distance of a centre.
domain_entries.BIO: A rounded anatomical part, as in the ball of the foot or a ball-and-socket joint.
domain_entries.REL: The object of play; "the ball is in your court" marks whose move it is.

count_condition: A round body or mass.
transfer_boundary: A mathematical ball includes its interior; a sphere is the surface only.

common_meaning: A formal social gathering for dancing.
example: They met at a charity ball.
rrgm_bridge: A social occasion with its own rules of dress and conduct.
invariant_mi: A formal social gathering for dancing.

domain_entries.REL: A ceremonial occasion marking status, season, or cause.

count_condition: A formal gathering whose main activity is dancing.
transfer_boundary: Unrelated to s1 in origin.

common_meaning: Heavy material carried in a ship or balloon to keep it stable; the gravel bed under a railway track; something that gives stability.
example: The ship took on water as ballast.
rrgm_bridge: Weight carried for steadiness alone. It earns its place by what does not happen.
invariant_mi: Added weight or resistance that steadies a system which would otherwise be unstable.

domain_entries.PHY: Mass placed low in a hull; crushed stone that spreads load and drains a track; a device limiting current in a lamp.
domain_entries.BIO: Ballast water carries organisms between seas and spreads invasive species.
domain_entries.LIN: Figurative: a steadying element in a person or institution.

count_condition: A system prone to instability, and added weight or resistance that steadies it.
transfer_boundary: Ballast is not cargo and not an anchor: it steadies a thing that is still moving. Not dead weight, which serves no purpose.

common_meaning: A thin rubber bag inflated with air or gas; a large bag filled with hot air or light gas that rises and carries passengers or instruments; to swell rapidly.
example: The weather balloon burst at thirty kilometres.
rrgm_bridge: An envelope shaped by what fills it, and carried by the difference between inside and outside.
invariant_mi: A flexible envelope that expands when filled with gas, and rises if the gas is lighter than the surrounding air.

domain_entries.PHY: A lighter-than-air craft lifted by buoyancy; an elastic membrane under internal pressure.
domain_entries.BIO: An inflatable device used to widen a vessel or passage.
domain_entries.ECO: A balloon payment: a large final instalment; costs that balloon grow out of control.
domain_entries.LIN: The outlined space holding a character's words in a comic.

count_condition: A flexible envelope, a filling gas, and expansion.
transfer_boundary: A balloon drifts; an airship is steered.

common_meaning: To prohibit officially; an official prohibition.
example: The city banned smoking in parks.
rrgm_bridge: Permission withdrawn by an authority. A ban given without notice also removes the banned party's chance to contest it.
invariant_mi: An official prohibition issued by an authority over a stated scope.

domain_entries.REL: A legal or institutional prohibition of an act, or exclusion of a person.
domain_entries.DIG: Blocking an account or address; a "shadow ban" restricts without telling the user.
domain_entries.ECO: Prohibition of trade in a good.
domain_entries.MYT: In several religious traditions, a formal curse or exclusion from the community.

count_condition: An authority, a scope, and a prohibited act or excluded party.
transfer_boundary: A ban is not a boycott (a voluntary refusal by many) or one party's refusal. Banning an act is different from banning a person.

common_meaning: A long curved fruit with yellow skin and soft sweet flesh; the plant that bears it.
example: She sliced a banana onto her cereal.
rrgm_bridge: A crop of near-identical clones, and so a standing example of uniformity bought at the cost of resilience.
invariant_mi: The elongated fruit of plants of the genus Musa, or the plant.

domain_entries.BIO: The plant is a giant herb; the main export variety is a sterile clone, vulnerable as a whole to a single disease.
domain_entries.ECO: A major traded crop; "banana republic" names a state dependent on one export controlled from abroad.
domain_entries.LIN: Idioms such as "go bananas".

count_condition: The fruit or plant of the genus.
transfer_boundary: Botanically a berry. Plantains are bananas used for cooking.

common_meaning: A flat strip or loop of material; a stripe; a range of values or frequencies.
example: The radio station moved to a different band.
rrgm_bridge: A bounded range along a scale. RRGM speaks of a mercy band: the range within which a thing still counts as itself despite change.
invariant_mi: A strip, or a bounded range along a scale.

domain_entries.PHY: A range of frequencies or energies, as in radio bands and the energy bands of a solid.
domain_entries.FOR: A defined range within a graded scheme, such as a tax band.
domain_entries.DIG: A communication channel; "out of band" means by a separate, independent channel.
domain_entries.BIO: A visible stripe marking a chromosome region or a separated molecule.

count_condition: A scale or surface, and a strip or range with two edges.
transfer_boundary: A band has edges, and what falls outside is out of band. Out-of-band confirmation is trusted because the channel is independent.

common_meaning: A group of musicians; a group of people with a common purpose.
example: The band played until midnight.
rrgm_bridge: A small group held together by shared activity.
invariant_mi: A group of people joined for a common purpose, especially musicians.

domain_entries.REL: A musical group; a small company; in anthropology, the smallest kind of foraging society.

count_condition: Several people and a shared purpose or activity.
transfer_boundary: A band in anthropology is not a tribe.

common_meaning: A strip of material used to bind a wound or protect an injured part of the body.
example: The nurse wrapped a bandage around his wrist.
rrgm_bridge: Protects the place of harm while repair goes on beneath. It is not the repair, and it does nothing about the cause.
invariant_mi: A strip of material bound round an injury to protect, support, or compress it.

domain_entries.BIO: Holds dressings in place, limits swelling, and supports injured parts.
domain_entries.LIN: Figurative: a superficial or temporary fix.

count_condition: An injury, a strip of material, and binding around the injured part.
transfer_boundary: A bandage is not a dressing, which touches the wound. Not a cast or a tourniquet.

common_meaning: The range of frequencies within a band; the amount of data a connection can carry in a given time; (informal) the capacity to deal with something.
example: Video calls need more bandwidth than email.
rrgm_bridge: A limit on how much difference can pass per unit of time. What exceeds it is lost or must wait.
invariant_mi: The width of the range a channel can carry, and so the rate at which it can carry information.

domain_entries.PHY: The difference between the highest and lowest frequencies of a signal or channel.
domain_entries.DIG: The maximum data rate of a link.
domain_entries.FOR: A term in the formula for channel capacity; a smoothing width in statistics.
domain_entries.COG: Figurative: available attention or mental capacity.

count_condition: A channel, and a measured range or maximum rate.
transfer_boundary: Bandwidth is not speed, delay, or actual throughput. "Mental bandwidth" is a metaphor.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: The punishment of being sent away from a place or community and forbidden to return.
example: Banishment from the city was the sentence for treason.
rrgm_bridge: Removes a member from the place where they are counted as belonging, while they go on existing elsewhere.
invariant_mi: Formal expulsion of a person or being from a place or community, with return forbidden.

domain_entries.MYT: Expulsions that found a new condition, such as the casting out from Eden or from heaven, told within particular traditions.
domain_entries.REL: Exile, ostracism, and outlawry as legal penalties.

count_condition: An expelling authority, an expelled party, a place or community, and a bar on return.
transfer_boundary: Banishment is not chosen exile, not imprisonment (which keeps in), and not exclusion from rites only.

common_meaning: A business that keeps and lends money; a store of something held for use.
example: She paid the cheque into the bank.
rrgm_bridge: Holds what others deposit and releases it on terms. It runs on the depositors' trust that what is held can be had back.
invariant_mi: An institution or store that holds deposits of something of value and lends or releases it.

domain_entries.ECO: A financial firm that takes deposits and makes loans.
domain_entries.BIO: A store of biological material such as blood, seeds, or tissue.
domain_entries.DIG: An organised store or set, such as a data bank or filter bank.
domain_entries.REL: "To bank on": to rely on.

count_condition: A holder, deposits by others, and release or lending on terms.
transfer_boundary: Deposits are mostly lent out and are not sitting in a vault. A bank is not a safe.

common_meaning: The land alongside a river or lake; a raised mass or slope; a row of similar things.
example: They picnicked on the river bank.
rrgm_bridge: An edge that contains a flow and is slowly reshaped by it.
invariant_mi: A raised or sloping margin or mass, especially the land at the edge of a river.

domain_entries.PHY: The margin of a channel; a mass of cloud or snow; the tilt of an aircraft or road in a turn.

count_condition: A margin, slope, or mass with a raised profile.
transfer_boundary: Left and right banks are named facing downstream.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: In Irish folklore, a female spirit whose wailing warns of a death in the family.
example: They said the banshee was heard the night before he died.
rrgm_bridge: A messenger of an event she does not bring about.
invariant_mi: In Irish tradition, a female spirit whose cry announces an imminent death in a family.

domain_entries.MYT: Attached to particular old families; her name means "woman of the fairy mound".

count_condition: An Irish or Irish-derived source.
transfer_boundary: The banshee announces death and does not cause it. Not the ghost of a dead person. The popular image of a screaming monster is a later simplification.

common_meaning: The playful and friendly exchange of teasing remarks.
example: There was good-natured banter between the two teams.
rrgm_bridge: Mock attack understood by both sides as play. It exists only while both sides take it that way.
invariant_mi: A light, playful exchange of teasing between parties who understand it as friendly.

domain_entries.LIN: A speech genre in which apparent rudeness signals closeness.
domain_entries.REL: A way of building and showing familiarity.

count_condition: Reciprocal teasing and a shared understanding that it is not serious.
transfer_boundary: Where one side does not take it as play, it is not banter. Saying "only banter" afterwards does not settle that.
