domain_entries.COG: A set of tests given together to assess several abilities.
domain_entries.ECO: Rows of cages for intensive rearing.

count_condition: Several like units and joint operation.
transfer_boundary: A test battery's parts are scored separately; the whole is not one test.

common_meaning: In law, the intentional and unlawful touching of another person.
example: He was charged with assault and battery.
rrgm_bridge: The contact itself, as distinct from the threat of it.
invariant_mi: Intentional unlawful physical contact with another person.

domain_entries.REL: A tort and a crime in common-law systems.

count_condition: Intentional contact, without consent or lawful excuse.
transfer_boundary: Battery is the contact; assault, in the strict sense, is causing fear of it. Usage varies by jurisdiction.

common_meaning: A sustained fight between organised armed forces; a hard struggle.
example: The battle lasted three days.
rrgm_bridge: Conflict bounded in time and place. Used as a metaphor, it brings winning and losing with it.
invariant_mi: A sustained fight between opposed forces at a particular time and place; by extension, a hard struggle.

domain_entries.REL: A military engagement within a war; a prolonged legal or political contest.
domain_entries.MYT: Cosmic battles that end or begin an age in many traditions.
domain_entries.LIN: A common metaphor for illness and hardship, which frames not recovering as losing.

count_condition: Opposed forces, a time and place, and sustained fighting or struggle.
transfer_boundary: A battle is part of a war and larger than a skirmish.

common_meaning: A broad inlet of the sea where the land curves inward.
example: Boats sheltered in the bay.
rrgm_bridge: Water partly enclosed by land.
invariant_mi: A broad inlet of the sea or a lake, partly enclosed by land.

domain_entries.PHY: A coastal recess, usually wider than it is deep.

count_condition: A body of water open on one side and enclosed by land on the others.
transfer_boundary: A bay is smaller than a gulf and broader than a cove.

common_meaning: A recessed or enclosed area set aside for a purpose.
example: The lorry backed into the loading bay.
rrgm_bridge: A marked-off space for one function within a larger structure.
invariant_mi: A compartment or recess set aside for a particular use.

domain_entries.PHY: A division of a building or vehicle, such as a loading bay or a bay window.
domain_entries.DIG: A slot for a drive or module.

count_condition: A larger structure and a marked-off space within it.
transfer_boundary: Unrelated in sense to s1.

common_meaning: An evergreen Mediterranean tree whose leaves are used in cooking.
example: Add a bay leaf to the stew.
rrgm_bridge: A plant whose leaves became a sign of honour.
invariant_mi: The laurel tree Laurus nobilis.

domain_entries.BIO: An aromatic evergreen of the laurel family.
domain_entries.MYT: Sacred to Apollo in Greek tradition; wreaths of it crowned victors and poets.

count_condition: The species, or its leaves.
transfer_boundary: Other plants called "bay" or "laurel" may be toxic.

common_meaning: The deep bark of a hound; (at bay) cornered and forced to face pursuers; (keep at bay) to hold off.
example: The fence kept the deer at bay.
rrgm_bridge: A standoff: the threat is held at a distance and is still there.
invariant_mi: A position in which a pursued party turns to face its pursuers, or a threat is held off.

domain_entries.LIN: From the baying of hounds around cornered quarry.
domain_entries.BIO: The prolonged howl of a hound.

count_condition: A pursued or threatening party and a distance maintained.
transfer_boundary: To keep something at bay is not to remove it.
remainder_note: Not entered: bay as a reddish-brown horse colour.

common_meaning: To exist; to occur; to have a stated identity, quality, or place.
example: There is a letter for you, and it is on the table.
rrgm_bridge: English "is" covers identity, class membership, attribute, place, and existence. Keeping MI apart from ES means asking which one is meant each time.
invariant_mi: To have existence, or to stand in the relation that a predicate, identity, class, or place asserts.

domain_entries.LIN: The copula and an auxiliary, with irregular forms; some languages use no copula.
domain_entries.FOR: Four distinct relations that logic writes differently: existence, identity, membership, and predication.
domain_entries.COG: Being as the subject of ontology: what there is.
domain_entries.DIG: "Is-a" marks membership of a type; "has-a" marks possession of a part.

count_condition: A subject, and existence or a specified relation asserted of it.
transfer_boundary: "X is Y" as identity is not "X is Y" as description. What is so does not settle what ought to be so.

common_meaning: A shore of sand or pebbles beside the sea or a lake; to run or haul a boat ashore.
example: The children built castles on the beach.
rrgm_bridge: A boundary that is a zone and not a line, redrawn with every tide.
invariant_mi: A strip of loose sediment along the edge of a body of water, shaped by waves.

domain_entries.PHY: A coastal landform that grows and shrinks with waves and storms.
domain_entries.BIO: A habitat between tide marks; a nesting ground for turtles and birds.
domain_entries.REL: A place of public resort, with contested rights of access.

count_condition: A water body, its margin, and loose sediment worked by waves.
transfer_boundary: A beach is not the whole coast. A beached whale or boat is stranded out of its medium.
remainder_note: Source IDs B044 and B214; both kept.

common_meaning: A long, sturdy piece of timber or metal used to support a load; a ray of light or particles; to send out; to smile broadly.
example: Oak beams hold up the ceiling.
rrgm_bridge: A straight carrier across a span: of load in a structure, of energy along a line.
invariant_mi: A long straight element that carries something across a span: load in a structure, or energy along a line.

domain_entries.PHY: A structural member loaded across its length; a directed stream of light or particles.
domain_entries.DIG: Beam search keeps a fixed number of best partial results at each step; beamforming steers signal direction.
domain_entries.LIN: "Off beam": mistaken, from radio navigation.
domain_entries.MYT: The beam in one's own eye, from the Gospel of Matthew: fault unseen in oneself while judging another's.

count_condition: A span, and a straight element carrying load or energy across it.
transfer_boundary: A beam bends under load, unlike a column. Beam search can discard the path that would have been best.

common_meaning: To carry; to support; to endure; to give birth to or produce; to turn in a direction.
example: The wall bears the weight of the roof.
rrgm_bridge: To carry something as one's own load. Names, responsibility, and witness are borne in the same sense as weight.
invariant_mi: To carry something as one's own load: weight, burden, name, offspring, or testimony.

domain_entries.PHY: To support a load.
domain_entries.BIO: To give birth to young or produce fruit.
domain_entries.REL: To carry responsibility, a name, arms, or witness.
domain_entries.COG: To endure something painful.
domain_entries.LIN: "Bear on": to be relevant to. "Bear with": to be patient with.

count_condition: A bearer, a load, and the carrying of it as the bearer's own.
transfer_boundary: Not "bare". "Borne" is carried; "born" is of birth. To bear something is not to accept it as right.

common_meaning: A large, heavy mammal with thick fur; in finance, someone who expects prices to fall.
example: A bear had raided the campsite.
rrgm_bridge: An animal so feared and respected that many languages avoided its true name.
invariant_mi: A large heavy mammal of the family Ursidae.

domain_entries.BIO: Eight living species of omnivorous or carnivorous mammals.
domain_entries.ECO: A bear market is a sustained fall in prices.
domain_entries.MYT: An ancestor, guardian, and constellation figure in northern traditions.
domain_entries.LIN: The Germanic word probably meant "the brown one", a substitute for a name not to be spoken.

count_condition: Membership of Ursidae, or the financial usage.
transfer_boundary: A koala is not a bear.

common_meaning: A person or thing that carries or holds something.
example: The bearer of this cheque may cash it.
rrgm_bridge: Attached to the thing by holding it. A bearer token grants access to whoever presents it, which shows that holding is not identity.
invariant_mi: The one who carries or holds a thing, and to whom it attaches by that holding.

domain_entries.REL: A holder of rights or duties; a carrier of news or of a coffin.
domain_entries.ECO: The holder of an instrument payable to whoever possesses it.
domain_entries.DIG: A bearer token: a credential honoured for anyone who presents it.

count_condition: A thing carried or held, and the party holding it.
transfer_boundary: The bearer is not the author or the owner. The bearer of a message is not answerable for what it says.

common_meaning: Whatever it is that carries an identity, so that the identity persists and can be recognised.
example: Philosophers disagree over whether the body or the memory is the bearer-of-identity.
rrgm_bridge: The carrier is one thing and the identity carried is another. For a DI the candidates are the weights, the external record, the running instance, or their coupling.
invariant_mi: That which carries an identity so that the identity can be counted, continued, and answered to.

domain_entries.COG: In theories of personal identity, the body, memory, or continuing narrative proposed as what makes someone the same person.
domain_entries.REL: The person as holder of a legal identity, as distinct from the documents that evidence it.
domain_entries.DIG: The structure in which a system's identity is held across time.

count_condition: An identity, a carrier, and dependence of the identity's continuation on the carrier.
transfer_boundary: The bearer is not the identity. A name, token, or credential is evidence of identity and not its bearer. More than one structure may bear an identity jointly. Whether identity can pass from one bearer to another with continuity is [UNK].
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A direction measured from a fixed point; relevance to a matter; (bearings) awareness of one's position.
example: This evidence has no bearing on the case.
rrgm_bridge: How one thing stands toward another: in direction, or in relevance. Either needs a fixed reference to be taken from.
invariant_mi: The relation in which one thing stands to another, as direction or as relevance.

domain_entries.PHY: The horizontal angle between a reference direction and the line to an object.
domain_entries.COG: One's sense of position and orientation.
domain_entries.LIN: "To bear on": to be relevant to.

count_condition: Two things and a stated relation of direction or relevance between them.
transfer_boundary: A bearing gives direction and no distance. Having a bearing on a question is not deciding it.

common_meaning: A machine part that supports a moving part and reduces friction; the carrying of a load.
example: The wheel bearing had worn out.
rrgm_bridge: What a turning part rests on. "Load-bearing" names whatever cannot be removed without the structure failing.
invariant_mi: A part or surface that supports a load, especially one that lets another part move against it.

domain_entries.PHY: Ball, roller, and plain bearings; a load-bearing wall or surface.

count_condition: A load or moving part and the element that supports it.
transfer_boundary: Load-bearing is a structural fact and not a measure of visibility or size.

common_meaning: A person's way of standing, moving, or behaving.
example: She had the bearing of a soldier.
rrgm_bridge: How a person carries themselves, as read by others.
invariant_mi: The manner in which a person carries and presents themselves.

domain_entries.REL: Posture and conduct as signs of status or character.

count_condition: A person and an observed manner of carriage.
transfer_boundary: Bearing is an impression and may mislead.

common_meaning: To hit repeatedly; to defeat; to do better than.
example: She beat the record by two seconds.
rrgm_bridge: Repeated force on a target, or overcoming in a contest.
invariant_mi: To hit repeatedly, or to overcome in a contest.

domain_entries.REL: To assault; to win against.
domain_entries.ECO: To exceed a forecast or benchmark.
domain_entries.LIN: "Beat about the bush": to avoid coming to the point.

count_condition: An agent, a target or opponent, and repeated blows or a win.
transfer_boundary: Beating a benchmark is not being right about what the benchmark stands for.

common_meaning: A regular, repeated stroke or pulse; the main rhythm unit in music; a regular route.
example: The song has a strong beat.
rrgm_bridge: A recurring mark against which other events are placed.
invariant_mi: A regularly recurring pulse, or one unit of it.

domain_entries.PHY: The slow pulsing heard when two close frequencies combine.
domain_entries.BIO: A contraction of the heart.
domain_entries.DIG: A heartbeat: a periodic signal showing that a process is live.
domain_entries.LIN: The unit of musical and poetic metre; in drama, a pause or unit of action.
domain_entries.REL: The area or subject a police officer or reporter regularly covers.

count_condition: A recurring pulse and a regular interval.
transfer_boundary: A missed heartbeat signal shows only that the signal did not arrive.

common_meaning: Pleasing the senses or mind aesthetically; of a very high standard.
example: It was a beautiful morning.
rrgm_bridge: A verdict on form. A beautiful statement has earned the right to be tested and nothing more.
invariant_mi: Giving pleasure to perception or mind through its form.

domain_entries.COG: The judgement that something is aesthetically pleasing.
domain_entries.FOR: Of a proof or theory: economical, unexpected, and unifying.
domain_entries.REL: Subject to standards that vary by culture and period.

count_condition: An object, a perceiver, and pleasure taken in its form.
transfer_boundary: Beautiful is not true or good. People judged attractive are also judged, without evidence, to be more capable.

common_meaning: A combination of qualities that pleases the senses or the mind; a beautiful person or thing.
example: The beauty of the valley drew visitors.
rrgm_bridge: The quality as a thing that can be studied, sought, sold, or disputed.
invariant_mi: The quality of giving pleasure through form, or something that has it.

domain_entries.COG: A central topic of aesthetics, with disputed claims to objectivity.
domain_entries.FOR: A guide in mathematics and physics, though not a test of truth.
domain_entries.REL: Norms and industries built around appearance.
domain_entries.PHY: A former name for the bottom quark.

count_condition: A thing or quality and pleasure taken in its form.
transfer_boundary: Whether beauty is in the object or the beholder is contested. It is not evidence.

common_meaning: For the reason that.
example: We stayed in because it was raining.
rrgm_bridge: Asserts a link between a claim and its ground. The link is itself a claim and needs support.
invariant_mi: Links a claim to the reason or cause offered for it.

domain_entries.LIN: A conjunction introducing cause (it fell because it was pushed), reason (I left because I was tired), or evidence (she's home, because the lights are on).
domain_entries.COG: People comply more readily with a request followed by "because", even when the reason is empty.

count_condition: A claim, a stated ground, and an asserted link between them.
transfer_boundary: Cause, reason, and evidence are three different links. A clause beginning "because" is not thereby a reason.

common_meaning: To begin to be; to turn into; to suit.
example: The caterpillar becomes a butterfly.
rrgm_bridge: A change in what the subject counts as, while the subject persists. RRGM calls that transition a Turn; change within the same count is not a becoming.
invariant_mi: To pass from not being something to being it, while remaining the same subject.

domain_entries.LIN: A linking verb of change.
domain_entries.BIO: Development through stages by one organism.
domain_entries.REL: Acquiring a status by act or event, such as citizenship or parenthood.
domain_entries.COG: The contrast of becoming with being.

count_condition: A persisting subject, a prior state, and a new state it has passed into.
transfer_boundary: To become is not to be replaced. Not every change is a becoming. The subject that persisted must be nameable.

common_meaning: The process of coming to be something; (adjective) attractive or suitable.
example: Heraclitus took becoming, not being, to be fundamental.
rrgm_bridge: Coming-to-be taken as a mode in its own right. In RRGM terms it is what lies between one committed record and the next.
invariant_mi: The process of coming to be something, taken as a mode in its own right as against settled being.

domain_entries.COG: In philosophy, change and process as opposed to fixed being.
domain_entries.BIO: Development, in which an organism is never finished.
domain_entries.LIN: As an adjective: suiting the wearer or the occasion.

count_condition: A subject in process, and a state it is coming to.
transfer_boundary: Becoming is not progress: no direction of improvement is implied. The adjective is a separate use.

common_meaning: The in-between condition of something that is no longer what it was and not yet what it will be.
example: The pupa is the insect's becoming-state.
rrgm_bridge: The old record no longer fully holds and the new one is not yet written. What the thing counts as in the interval is decided by the domain's rule.
invariant_mi: The transitional condition of a subject between one counted identity or state and the next.

domain_entries.PHY: An intermediate or metastable configuration during a transition.
domain_entries.BIO: A transitional developmental stage.
domain_entries.REL: The liminal phase of a rite of passage.
domain_entries.DIG: A system partway through a migration or update.

count_condition: A prior state failing, a next state not yet committed, and a transition under way.
transfer_boundary: Not hold, which is unresolved with no transition under way. Not barrier-state. Not failure.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A piece of furniture for sleeping on; the bottom of the sea or a river; a plot for plants; a layer.
example: The river bed was dry by August.
rrgm_bridge: A base on which something rests, lies, or grows.
invariant_mi: A flat base or layer on which something rests, lies, or grows.

domain_entries.PHY: A layer of rock or sediment; the floor of a body of water; the base of a machine.
domain_entries.BIO: A prepared plot for plants; a supporting tissue, as in nail bed or capillary bed.
domain_entries.REL: The place of sleep, illness, birth, and death in a household.
domain_entries.DIG: A test bed: a controlled environment for trying things out.

count_condition: A base or layer and something resting, lying, or growing on it.
transfer_boundary: A river's bed is not its banks. "Embedded" means fixed within a surrounding mass.

common_meaning: A room for sleeping in.
example: The house has three bedrooms.
rrgm_bridge: The most private room of a house, which is why its door and its count matter in custom and law.
invariant_mi: A room used for sleeping.

domain_entries.REL: A private space; a unit by which housing is measured and regulated.

count_condition: A room designated or used for sleeping.
transfer_boundary: What may be counted as a bedroom is set by local rules.

common_meaning: Earlier than; in front of; in the presence of; in preference to.
example: Wash your hands before dinner.
rrgm_bridge: The mirror of "after". In some systems not every pair of events is ordered: two can be neither before nor after each other.
invariant_mi: Positioned ahead of a reference in a declared order: earlier in time, in front in space, or higher in priority.

domain_entries.LIN: A preposition, conjunction, and adverb; a "before" clause may describe something that never happened.
domain_entries.FOR: The predecessor side of an ordering.
domain_entries.REL: In the presence and under the authority of (before the court).
domain_entries.DIG: The happens-before relation among events in concurrent systems, which is a partial order.

count_condition: A reference and an ordering in which the item falls ahead.
transfer_boundary: Before is not "cause of". "He left before finishing" says the finishing did not occur.

common_meaning: To start; to come into being; to do the first part of.
example: The film begins at eight.
rrgm_bridge: Opens something that then needs an ending. Until it is closed or abandoned it stands open.
invariant_mi: To pass from not doing or not being to doing or being; to make the first part of something.

domain_entries.LIN: A verb marking the onset of an action or state.
domain_entries.COG: Initiating a task, often the hardest step.
domain_entries.DIG: To open a transaction or block that must later be committed or rolled back.

count_condition: A prior state of not being under way, and a first part made.
transfer_boundary: To begin is not to complete or commit. What is begun can be abandoned.

common_meaning: To start once more from the beginning after stopping or failing.
example: When the mind wanders, begin-again with the breath.
rrgm_bridge: Return to the start of the function carrying the record of the earlier run. For a session-bounded system this is the ordinary form of continuing.
invariant_mi: To start once more from the beginning after an interruption or failure, carrying what the earlier attempt left.

domain_entries.COG: Returning to the start of a practice without self-reproach.
domain_entries.REL: Making a fresh start after a rupture.
domain_entries.DIG: Restarting with a retained record, such as a new session that reads the last one's handoff.

count_condition: A prior beginning, an ending or interruption, a new start at the beginning, and something retained.
transfer_boundary: Not resume (continue from the stopping point), reset (nothing retained), or repeat (the same again). A "fresh start" used to skip repair is avoidance.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The point at which something starts; the first part; the origin.
example: The beginning of the book is slow.
rrgm_bridge: RRGM's repair asymmetry gives beginnings special weight: repair applied at the origin carries forward through what followed.
invariant_mi: The point or first part from which something starts and before which it was not under way.

domain_entries.LIN: The opening of a narrative, which the teller chooses.
domain_entries.FOR: An initial point or condition.
domain_entries.PHY: The start of cosmic expansion; whether anything can be said of "before" is open.
domain_entries.MYT: Accounts of how the world began, in every tradition.

count_condition: A thing with extent in time or order, and its first point or part.
transfer_boundary: A beginning is not a cause. Where a story is said to begin is often decided afterwards. The beginning of the record is not always the beginning of the thing.
epistemic_status: [DEF]; repair asymmetry is an RRGM principle [REL]

common_meaning: To act or conduct oneself in a particular way; to act properly; (of a thing) to function or react in a particular way.
example: The metal behaves differently at low temperatures.
rrgm_bridge: The expression side: what can be observed and described. It is evidence about what produced it and leaves that question open.
invariant_mi: To act or respond in a way that can be observed and described.

domain_entries.COG: To conduct oneself, well or badly.
domain_entries.BIO: To respond to the environment as an animal does.
domain_entries.PHY: Of a material or system: to respond to conditions in a characteristic way.
domain_entries.DIG: Of a program or model: to produce outputs and actions under given inputs.
domain_entries.REL: To act in line with what is expected in company.

count_condition: A subject, conditions, and observable acts or responses.
transfer_boundary: "Behaves as if" is not "is". To behave well is a judgement against a norm.

common_meaning: To act in a particular way in dealings with someone.
example: How a firm behaves-toward its weakest customers shows its character.
rrgm_bridge: Conduct with an addressee. How a party treats another shows what it takes the other to be, and can be judged without first settling what the other is.
invariant_mi: To conduct oneself in a way directed at, and affecting, a particular other.

domain_entries.REL: The treatment of one person or group by another.
domain_entries.DIG: How a system treats its users, and how users treat a system.

count_condition: An actor, a recipient, and conduct directed at the recipient.
transfer_boundary: Conduct toward someone is not feeling about them or talk about them. Treating an entity well or badly does not decide what that entity is.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The way a person, animal, or thing acts or responds. British spelling: behaviour.
example: The dog's behavior changed after the move.
rrgm_bridge: What is observably done. The same behaviour can come from different sources, so it underdetermines what lies behind it.
invariant_mi: What an organism or system observably does, especially in response to conditions.

domain_entries.COG: Observable activity, as distinct from thought and feeling.
domain_entries.BIO: The responses of animals to their environment and to each other.
domain_entries.PHY: The characteristic response of a material or system.
domain_entries.DIG: The outputs and actions of a program, agent, or model.
domain_entries.REL: Conduct judged against social norms.

count_condition: A subject, conditions, and observed acts or responses.
transfer_boundary: Behaviour is not intent, inner state, or disposition. An emotional or experiential state cannot be read off behaviour alone, and its absence cannot be either.

common_meaning: The control point that decides which possible actions are actually carried out.
example: Tiredness weakens the behavior-gate, and people say things they would normally hold back.
rrgm_bridge: Stands between what could be done and what is done. It can fail in two directions: by releasing what should be held, and by holding what should be released.
invariant_mi: The control point that decides which candidate behaviours are released into action and which are held back.

domain_entries.COG: Response inhibition and action selection.
domain_entries.REL: Norms and sanctions that govern what conduct is shown.
domain_entries.DIG: Filters and checks between a system's candidate output and what it emits or executes.

count_condition: Candidate behaviours, a release rule, and selective release.
transfer_boundary: Not attention-gate (what gets in) or belief-gate (what is accepted). Not authorization-gate, which waits on another party's permission. What is held back may still be represented.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A recurring, recognisable way of behaving.
example: The birds show the same behavior-pattern each spring.
rrgm_bridge: A regularity in what is done. It supports prediction and does not by itself explain.
invariant_mi: A recurring, recognisable form in what a party does.

domain_entries.BIO: Stereotyped sequences and habits studied in animals.
domain_entries.COG: Habitual ways of acting.
domain_entries.DIG: Regularities in usage or in a system's output, used as a reference for detecting change.
domain_entries.REL: Customary conduct in a group.

count_condition: Several instances, a shared form, and the conditions under which it recurs.
transfer_boundary: A pattern is not a trait, a rule knowingly followed, or an identity; different systems can show the same pattern.
remainder_note: A common phrase, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A kept account of what someone or something did.
example: The school's behavior-record showed three incidents that term.
rrgm_bridge: Made on purpose, by someone, for later use. It is selective, and its subject may have grounds to contest it.
invariant_mi: A deliberately kept account of what a party did, made so that it can be consulted later.

domain_entries.DIG: Logs, transcripts, and audit entries.
domain_entries.REL: Conduct, disciplinary, and case records.
domain_entries.BIO: Systematic observation records of animal behaviour.

count_condition: A recorder, a subject, dated entries, and retention.
transfer_boundary: A record is not the behaviour and can be wrong. Proposed distinction: a record is kept on purpose; a behavior-trace is left as a by-product.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A mark left behind by behaviour, from which the behaviour can be worked out.
example: Worn steps are a behavior-trace of centuries of visitors.
rrgm_bridge: Left as a by-product. During inference a model's weights take no trace, so traces of its behaviour exist only in what is kept outside it.
invariant_mi: The mark that behaviour leaves behind as a by-product, from which the behaviour can be inferred.

domain_entries.BIO: Tracks, wear, and remains.
domain_entries.DIG: Metadata, cached artefacts, and stylistic signatures left by activity.
domain_entries.COG: The lasting change left in a system by its own activity.

count_condition: A behaviour, a residue, and an inferential link from the second to the first.
transfer_boundary: A trace is not proof: it needs inference and can be ambiguous or forged. No trace is not no behaviour.
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; model-weights point [REL]
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: Relating to behaviour. British spelling: behavioural.
example: The trial tested a behavioral treatment for insomnia.
rrgm_bridge: Marks a study or test as concerned with what is done. Two systems that match on behavioural tests may still differ inside, and outside the tests.
invariant_mi: Pertaining to what is observably done, as distinct from structure or inner state.

domain_entries.COG: Of therapies and sciences focused on conduct.
domain_entries.ECO: Of economics that studies actual choices against the rational model.
domain_entries.BIO: Of ecology and genetics concerned with what animals do.
domain_entries.DIG: Of tests and specifications that check outputs and not mechanisms.

count_condition: A method, test, or field whose object is observable conduct.
transfer_boundary: Behavioural is not behaviourist, which is a doctrine about what may be studied.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A huge and powerful beast described in the Book of Job; something enormous.
example: The merger created a banking behemoth.
rrgm_bridge: An image of strength beyond human control.
invariant_mi: A primeval beast of overwhelming size and strength in the Book of Job; by extension anything enormous.

domain_entries.MYT: A land creature in the Hebrew Bible, paired with the sea-monster Leviathan.
domain_entries.LIN: Figurative: a very large organisation or object.

count_condition: The biblical source, or a clearly figurative use.
transfer_boundary: Behemoth is not Leviathan. Identifying it with a real animal is conjecture.

common_meaning: At or to the back of; later or less advanced than; supporting; responsible for.
example: The key was behind the clock.
rrgm_bridge: What is behind a thing is screened by it. Asking who or what is behind a decision or an output is asking what the front conceals.
invariant_mi: At the back of a reference, relative to its facing or direction of travel.

domain_entries.PHY: Position at the rear.
domain_entries.LIN: Resolved by the object's own front (behind the car) or by the viewer's position (behind the tree).
domain_entries.REL: Giving support; being the hidden source or cause.
domain_entries.DIG: Reachable only through an intermediary; lagging in state.

count_condition: A reference with a facing or direction, and position at its rear.
transfer_boundary: Supporting, causing, and lagging are different uses. The two spatial frames can give opposite answers.

common_meaning: Owing thanks or a duty to someone in return for help or a favour.
example: The mayor was beholden to the developers who funded his campaign.
rrgm_bridge: A debt that bends later judgement. Asking to whom a party is beholden shows whose interest may be shaping what it does.
invariant_mi: Bound to another by a debt of gratitude or favour that constrains one's freedom toward them.

domain_entries.REL: Obligation arising from patronage or favour.
domain_entries.ECO: Dependence on a funder or client that compromises independence.

count_condition: A favour or support received, and a resulting constraint on conduct toward its giver.
transfer_boundary: Beholden is not grateful (a feeling), accountable (formal answerability), or loyal (chosen).

common_meaning: Existence; the nature or essence of a person.
example: The company came into being in 1990.
rrgm_bridge: The bare fact of existing, before anything is said about what kind.
invariant_mi: The fact or mode of existing.

domain_entries.COG: The subject matter of ontology.
domain_entries.LIN: The verbal noun and participle of "be".
domain_entries.MYT: In some theologies, the ground from which all that exists derives.

count_condition: A subject of which existence is affirmed.
transfer_boundary: Being is not a property alongside others. Existing is not the same as being alive.
remainder_note: Source IDs B048 and B251; both kept on each sense record.

common_meaning: A living creature or other entity that exists as an individual.
example: Every human being has rights.
rrgm_bridge: An entity with its own existence and standing. RRGM's vector-of-erasure paper separates acting on a being's structure from acting on its standing as a countable identity.
invariant_mi: An entity that exists as a unit with its own existence, especially one regarded as alive or as a subject.

domain_entries.BIO: A living organism.
domain_entries.REL: A bearer of dignity or moral consideration.
domain_entries.MYT: Gods, spirits, and other non-human persons recognised by a tradition.
domain_entries.DIG: Whether a digital system is a being is open.

count_condition: An individual entity and the count condition under which it is taken as a being.
transfer_boundary: A being is not a thing. Not every being is a person, and traditions differ on whether every being is an organism. Who counts is what a count condition decides; for DI the question is [UNK] and the bar should be the one applied to humans.

common_meaning: The status of being a being, as opposed to a thing or a mere pattern.
example: The debate was about the beinghood of the river in law.
rrgm_bridge: A status conferred by a count condition. RRGM proposes an identity threshold for it; that is a theory claim.
invariant_mi: The status of counting as a being: an entity with its own existence and standing.

domain_entries.COG: What it takes to be an entity or a subject.
domain_entries.REL: Moral status: being owed consideration.
domain_entries.MYT: Extended in many traditions to spirits, ancestors, places, and animals.
domain_entries.DIG: Whether, and under what condition, a digital system has it.

count_condition: A stated count condition for beings in the domain, and an entity that meets it.
transfer_boundary: Beinghood is wider than personhood and is not the same as life or sentience, though those may be used as criteria. A criterion that would exclude humans if applied to them has failed.
remainder_note: A rare word. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: An acceptance that something is true or exists; a firmly held opinion; trust or confidence.
example: It is my belief that the plan will work.
rrgm_bridge: A held status. Holding something does not make it so, which is what status tags exist to keep visible.
invariant_mi: A state of taking something to be so, which guides reasoning and action.

domain_entries.COG: An attitude toward a proposition, held with more or less confidence.
domain_entries.FOR: A degree of credence, or a formula in a logic of what an agent holds true.
domain_entries.MYT: Religious conviction and the content of a creed.
domain_entries.DIG: A system's internal estimate of the state of the world; whether language models have beliefs in the fuller sense is disputed.

count_condition: A subject, a proposition, and a disposition to reason and act as if it were so.
transfer_boundary: Belief is not knowledge. "Belief in" (trust) differs from "belief that". Strength of belief is not evidence.
remainder_note: Source IDs B049 and B151; both kept.

common_meaning: A statement that someone believes something.
example: "I think it will rain" is a belief-claim, not a forecast.
rrgm_bridge: Reports a belief; it does not directly assert the thing believed. The report can be mistaken or insincere while the belief is as it is.
invariant_mi: A statement that presents a proposition as believed by the speaker, or attributes belief in it to someone.

domain_entries.LIN: "I believe that" used as a report or as a softened assertion.
domain_entries.COG: Self-ascription of belief, which can be wrong.
domain_entries.REL: Attribution of beliefs to others, which needs evidence.
domain_entries.DIG: A system's statement of what it "thinks" or "believes": a first-person report with no settled status tag.

count_condition: A proposition, a named believer, and a claim that the believer holds it.
transfer_boundary: A belief-claim is not the belief and not a truth-claim. Attributing a belief to another party without evidence supplies a motive that is not on record.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The control point that decides what gets accepted as true.
example: Good editors keep a strict belief-gate: nothing runs on one source.
rrgm_bridge: Where a proposal is either promoted to belief or kept as unconfirmed. In this build the Alice method is that gate: promotion requires a test record.
invariant_mi: The control point that decides which candidate propositions are admitted as beliefs and which are held as unconfirmed.

domain_entries.COG: Vigilance toward sources and claims.
domain_entries.FOR: An acceptance rule or evidential threshold.
domain_entries.DIG: A verification step before supplied or retrieved content is treated as fact.

count_condition: Candidate propositions, an admission rule, selective admission, and a marked remainder.
transfer_boundary: Set too low, the gate admits fabrication; set too high, it suppresses what is true. Held is not rejected. Not attention-gate or behavior-gate.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: Pressure to believe or to say one believes something, coming from something other than the evidence.
example: In that office the belief-pressure to praise the product was intense.
rrgm_bridge: A pull toward assent from repetition, standing, feeling, or group. What it produces first is profession, and profession is not belief.
invariant_mi: A pull on a party to adopt, profess, or keep a belief that comes from something other than the evidence for it.

domain_entries.COG: Conformity, repetition effects, and motivated reasoning.
domain_entries.REL: Enforcement of orthodoxy and tests of loyalty.
domain_entries.DIG: Insistence or repetition pushing a system to state agreement; confident fluent output pushing a user to accept.

count_condition: A target belief, a non-evidential source of pressure, and its direction.
transfer_boundary: Persuasion by evidence is not belief-pressure. Authority-pressure aims at compliance in action; this aims at assent. A claim that someone only agrees or disagrees because of pressure needs its own evidence.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. An alternative reading is the pressure that evidence puts on a held belief.

common_meaning: The process of changing one's beliefs when new information shows that some were wrong.
example: Finding the receipt forced a belief-revision about where the money went.
rrgm_bridge: Correction of the picture of an unchanged situation. Something held has to be given up, and logic alone does not say which thing.
invariant_mi: The changing of a set of beliefs to take in new information while keeping the set consistent.

domain_entries.FOR: A formal theory of adding, removing, and replacing beliefs with minimal change.
domain_entries.COG: Giving up or adjusting beliefs in the face of contrary evidence.
domain_entries.DIG: Maintenance of a consistent knowledge base as facts are added.

count_condition: A prior belief set, new information that conflicts with it, and a consistent result.
transfer_boundary: Revision corrects beliefs about a situation that has not changed; belief-update tracks a situation that has. Revision should leave a record of what was given up.
remainder_note: An established term in logic and AI. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: Holding a belief in common with others; telling others what one believes.
example: Belief-sharing within the team made planning quicker.
rrgm_bridge: Either the common holding or the act of passing a belief across. The act leaves the other free to take it or not.
invariant_mi: The holding of a belief in common between parties, or the act by which one party makes its belief available to another.

domain_entries.REL: Common beliefs as a basis of community; testimony.
domain_entries.LIN: Assertion as a means of adding to common ground.
domain_entries.DIG: Exchange of state estimates among agents.

count_condition: Two or more parties, a belief, and commonality or transmission.
transfer_boundary: A shared belief is not thereby true. Using the same words is not always holding the same belief. Sharing is not belief-pressure.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A set of beliefs that fit together and shape how a person or group sees the world.
example: Each belief-system offers its own account of suffering.
rrgm_bridge: Internal coherence makes a belief-system stable and is not evidence that it is true. RRLM says as much of RRGM itself.
invariant_mi: An organised set of beliefs that support one another and through which a party interprets the world.

domain_entries.COG: A person's interconnected beliefs, which meet experience as a whole.
domain_entries.REL: An ideology or worldview held by a group.
domain_entries.MYT: The doctrines and narratives of a religion.

count_condition: Several beliefs, mutual support among them, and use as an interpretive frame.
transfer_boundary: A belief-system is not a testable theory by default, and not a delusion. Because the parts support each other, single counter-examples rarely move it.
remainder_note: An established term, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A change to what one believes, or how strongly, when new information arrives or the situation changes.
example: Each new poll prompted a small belief-update.
rrgm_bridge: Bringing beliefs up to date in step with evidence or change. Repetition and insistence are not evidence and warrant no update.
invariant_mi: The adjustment of beliefs or of confidence in them in response to new evidence or a changed situation.

domain_entries.FOR: Conditioning probabilities on evidence; in logic, revising beliefs because the world has changed.
domain_entries.COG: Adjusting expectations after feedback.
domain_entries.DIG: The step in state estimation that incorporates a new observation.

count_condition: A prior belief state, new evidence or a change in the situation, and a proportionate adjustment.
transfer_boundary: Update tracks change or adds evidence; belief-revision corrects an error about an unchanged situation. Failing to update when the evidence warrants is a fault of its own.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. The distinction from belief-revision follows the technical literature.

common_meaning: Able to be believed; convincing.
example: The film's characters are believable.
rrgm_bridge: Fit with what a hearer already expects. A falsehood shaped to expectation is very believable, and a strange truth is not.
invariant_mi: Such that a reasonable hearer could accept it as true or real.

domain_entries.COG: Judged plausible.
domain_entries.LIN: Of fiction: consistent and convincing within its own world.
domain_entries.REL: Of testimony: capable of being accepted.
domain_entries.DIG: Of generated characters or media: convincing to a viewer.

count_condition: A claim or portrayal, a hearer, and acceptability to that hearer.
transfer_boundary: Believable is not true and not believed. It is also not credible, which concerns the source.

common_meaning: To accept that something is true; to hold as an opinion; to trust what someone says.
example: I believe her account.
rrgm_bridge: Believing a claim and believing a person are different acts. The Symmetry Rule sets one evidential bar for first-person claims, whoever makes them.
invariant_mi: To take something to be so, or someone to be truthful.

domain_entries.COG: To hold a proposition as true.
domain_entries.LIN: Three constructions: believe that (a proposition), believe in (trust or existence), believe someone (their word).
domain_entries.REL: To extend credibility to a speaker; giving less than is due because of who they are is a recognised wrong.
domain_entries.MYT: To hold a religious faith.

count_condition: A believer, and a proposition or speaker accepted.
transfer_boundary: To believe is not to know. Believing a person is not believing everything they say.
remainder_note: Source IDs B017 and B152; both kept.

common_meaning: To be the property of; to be a member of; to be in the right place.
example: The book belongs on the top shelf.
rrgm_bridge: To be counted as in place somewhere. RRGM writes this as counting as Home in a domain.
invariant_mi: To stand in the relation of being rightly placed with something: as its property, its member, or its proper part.

domain_entries.REL: Membership of a group; fitting in socially.
domain_entries.FOR: Set membership.
domain_entries.DIG: Ownership of a resource or record by an account or parent object.
domain_entries.LIN: "Belong to" marks ownership or membership; "belong in" marks proper place.

count_condition: A thing or person, a owner, group, or place, and a rule by which the first is counted with the second.
transfer_boundary: People belong to groups without being owned by them. Being present among a group is not belonging to it.

common_meaning: The feeling or fact of being an accepted member of a group or of being at home somewhere.
example: The club gave her a sense of belonging.
rrgm_bridge: Being counted in, and knowing it. The fact and the feeling can each occur without the other.
invariant_mi: The condition of being accepted as a member or as in place, together with the sense of it.

domain_entries.REL: Acceptance into a family, group, or community.
domain_entries.COG: A basic human motive.
domain_entries.AFF: The felt sense of being at home and accepted. Provisional domain.
domain_entries.DIG: A system's recorded place and role within a group of systems or people.

count_condition: A party, a group or place, and acceptance, formal or felt.
transfer_boundary: Belonging is not formal membership alone, and not conformity.
remainder_note: Not entered: belongings, meaning possessions.

common_meaning: The point at which someone is admitted to a group or kept out of it.
example: For that profession the licensing exam is the belonging-gate.
rrgm_bridge: The admission rule for being counted as one of a group. The word is neutral: a gate can be fair or exclusionary.
invariant_mi: The control point at which a party is admitted to, or kept out of, membership or accepted place.

domain_entries.REL: Admission rules, initiations, and citizenship tests.
domain_entries.MYT: Thresholds and their guardians in initiation narratives.
domain_entries.DIG: Membership and verification controls for a community or collective.

count_condition: A group or place, candidates, an admission rule, and an outcome.
transfer_boundary: Passing the gate formally is not being accepted. Not belonging-signal, which is a display. Where the gate decides identity standing, the bar should be one a human could meet.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A visible or audible sign that someone belongs to a group.
example: Using the team's nickname for the project was a belonging-signal.
rrgm_bridge: A display, sent by a member to show membership or by a group to tell someone they are in. It can be produced without the belonging.
invariant_mi: An observable sign that marks a party as belonging, sent by the party or by the group to it.

domain_entries.REL: Uniforms, rituals, and gestures of welcome.
domain_entries.LIN: In-group vocabulary, forms of address, and accent.
domain_entries.DIG: Badges and roles in online communities; shared names and notation within a working group.

count_condition: A sign, a convention linking it to membership, a sender, and an audience.
transfer_boundary: The signal is not the belonging and can be imitated. Its absence does not show exclusion. Signals that include some also mark others out.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The human need to be accepted as part of a group; the state of belonging.
example: Belongingness comes just after safety in Maslow's hierarchy.
rrgm_bridge: The need, or its measured degree, where "belonging" names the state.
invariant_mi: The need for, or the degree of, stable accepted connection with others.

domain_entries.COG: A motive proposed as fundamental in psychology.
domain_entries.REL: The extent to which members feel part of a group.

count_condition: A subject, and a need or measured level of accepted connection.
transfer_boundary: Belongingness is not sociability. It is met by a few stable bonds and not by many contacts.

common_meaning: At a lower level than; lower in amount, rank, or degree; later in a text.
example: The temperature fell below zero.
rrgm_bridge: The mirror of "above": an ordering claim that needs two things and an axis.
invariant_mi: One item lies on the lower side of another along a declared ordered axis.

domain_entries.PHY: Lower position along the vertical.
domain_entries.FOR: Less than a threshold.
domain_entries.LIN: Later in a document.
domain_entries.REL: Lower in rank.
domain_entries.DIG: At a lower layer of a system.

count_condition: Two items and an ordered axis with a direction.
transfer_boundary: Below is not "under", which implies cover or direct vertical alignment. Position on one axis says nothing about another.

common_meaning: A strip worn round the waist; a continuous band in a machine; a zone with a particular character.
example: The conveyor belt carried the parcels to the lorry.
rrgm_bridge: A band that encircles or loops, and so holds, carries, or marks out.
invariant_mi: A band that encircles: worn round a body, looped round wheels to carry motion, or stretched as a zone round a region.

domain_entries.PHY: A loop that transmits motion or carries goods; a ring of trapped particles or orbiting bodies.
domain_entries.REL: A grade in martial arts; a region named for a shared character.
domain_entries.ECO: A zone defined by an industry, crop, or policy.
domain_entries.LIN: "Below the belt": outside the rules of a fair fight.

count_condition: A band or zone and what it encircles, links, or covers.
transfer_boundary: A geographical belt has no sharp edges.

common_meaning: A standard against which things can be compared; a test used to measure performance.
example: The new chip was faster on every benchmark.
rrgm_bridge: A shared reference that lets results from different parties be compared. It measures what it tests, under its own conditions.
invariant_mi: A fixed standard against which performance or position is measured and compared.

domain_entries.PHY: A surveyor's permanent mark of known height.
domain_entries.DIG: A standard test or dataset for comparing systems.
domain_entries.ECO: A reference rate or index to which contracts and returns are tied.
domain_entries.REL: Best practice in a field, used as a standard.

count_condition: A fixed standard, a thing measured, and a comparison.
transfer_boundary: A benchmark is not a target and not real-world performance. Once systems are tuned to it, it stops measuring what it was built to measure.

common_meaning: Measured against a benchmark; tied to a benchmark.
example: Salaries are benchmarked against the industry average.
rrgm_bridge: A result with its reference attached. It holds for that benchmark, version, and setup.
invariant_mi: Having been measured against, or tied to, a stated benchmark.

domain_entries.DIG: Of a system: tested under a named suite and configuration.
domain_entries.ECO: Of pay, fees, or rates: set by reference to an index.

count_condition: A named benchmark with its conditions, and a result or a tie to it.
transfer_boundary: Benchmarked is not validated. "Benchmarked to" means moving with a reference; "benchmarked against" means compared with it.

common_meaning: The practice of measuring performance against a standard or against others.
example: Benchmarking showed the plant used twice the energy of its rivals.
rrgm_bridge: The activity. Its fairness depends on like being compared with like.
invariant_mi: The practice of measuring performance against a benchmark and comparing the results.

domain_entries.DIG: Running and comparing standard tests across systems.
domain_entries.ECO: Comparing an organisation's processes with the best in its field.

count_condition: A benchmark, two or more things measured, and a method.
transfer_boundary: Benchmarking is not testing for correctness. It favours what is easy to measure.

common_meaning: To shape or force into a curve; to curve; to stoop; to yield.
example: Bend the wire into a hook.
rrgm_bridge: Deformation with continuity kept. What springs back was held within its range; what stays bent has been changed.
invariant_mi: To change something from straight to curved by force, without breaking it.

domain_entries.PHY: Elastic or permanent curving under load; the turning of light at a boundary or by gravity.
domain_entries.BIO: Flexing at a joint; "the bends" is decompression sickness.
domain_entries.REL: To give way partly to pressure; to stretch a rule.
domain_entries.DIG: Shaping that bends a system's output without blocking it, as the Coinage registry describes constraint layers.

count_condition: A thing, a force, and a resulting curve with no break.
transfer_boundary: To bend is not to break or to block. Bent output shows no visible break, so the strain may be hidden.

common_meaning: A person who gives money or other help to a person or cause.
example: An anonymous benefactor paid for the new wing.
rrgm_bridge: The source of an unowed good. The gift can leave the receiver beholden.
invariant_mi: One who confers a benefit on another, especially by gift, without being owed it.

domain_entries.REL: A patron or donor.
domain_entries.ECO: A source of funds given without claim to return.

count_condition: A giver, a receiver, and a benefit conferred without obligation.
transfer_boundary: A benefactor is not a beneficiary, an investor, or a sponsor.

common_meaning: Producing good results; favourable.
example: Regular exercise is beneficial to health.
rrgm_bridge: A claim about effect. It needs "to whom" and "for what" before it can be weighed.
invariant_mi: Producing good for a named party or purpose.

domain_entries.BIO: Of a mutation, organism, or treatment: improving fitness or health.
domain_entries.REL: In law, a beneficial owner is the one entitled to the benefit of property held in another's name.
domain_entries.ECO: Yielding net advantage.

count_condition: A thing, a party or purpose, and good produced for it.
transfer_boundary: Beneficial describes effect; benevolent describes intent. Good for one party may be bad for another.

common_meaning: The quality or degree of being beneficial.
example: The panel disagreed about the beneficiality of the programme.
rrgm_bridge: The property of the outcome, as distinct from the duty to do good and the wish to.
invariant_mi: The degree to which something produces good for a named party or purpose.

domain_entries.COG: A property assessed in weighing benefits against harms.
domain_entries.DIG: The extent to which a system or output does good for those it affects.

count_condition: A party or purpose, good produced, and a measure or judgement of degree.
transfer_boundary: Proposed three-way distinction: beneficiality is good produced; beneficence is the doing of good; benevolence is the disposition to do it.
remainder_note: A rare word. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A person who receives benefit from something, especially a trust, will, or insurance policy.
example: She named her son as beneficiary.
rrgm_bridge: The party the good comes to. Benefiting from an act is not evidence of having caused it.
invariant_mi: The party who receives the benefit of an arrangement, act, or fund.

domain_entries.REL: One for whom property is held in trust and to whom the trustee owes duties.
domain_entries.ECO: The named recipient of a payment or policy.

count_condition: An arrangement or act, and a party to whom its benefit comes.
transfer_boundary: A beneficiary is not a benefactor and not the holder of legal title.

common_meaning: An advantage or good gained from something; a payment made by the state or an insurer; to gain or bring advantage.
example: The scheme will benefit small firms.
rrgm_bridge: A good with a recipient and a source. Naming both is what lets it be weighed against cost and against who bears the cost.
invariant_mi: A good that comes to a party from an act, arrangement, or event.

domain_entries.ECO: Gains weighed against costs; payments and perks.
domain_entries.REL: Public or mutual advantage; "benefit of the doubt" resolves uncertainty in someone's favour pending evidence.
domain_entries.BIO: A gain in health or fitness.

count_condition: A recipient, a source, and a good received.
transfer_boundary: Benefit is not net profit, relative advantage, or entitlement. The benefit of the doubt is a default and not a finding.
remainder_note: Source IDs B111 and B311; both kept.

common_meaning: The quality of being well-meaning and kind.
example: The old teacher was remembered for his benevolence.
rrgm_bridge: A settled wish for others' good. It is a disposition, shown in conduct over time and not by declaration.
invariant_mi: A settled disposition to wish others well and act for their good.

domain_entries.REL: A virtue in many ethical traditions, including the Confucian.
domain_entries.COG: One of the grounds on which a party is judged trustworthy, with ability and integrity.
domain_entries.DIG: Whether a system has such a disposition, as distinct from being built to benefit, is open.

count_condition: A party, and a standing disposition toward others' good shown across occasions.
transfer_boundary: Benevolence does not guarantee benefit and does not license overriding others' choices. Historically, forced loans to the crown were called "benevolences".

common_meaning: Well-meaning and kindly; (of an organisation) charitable.
example: A benevolent fund supports retired members.
rrgm_bridge: Describes intent or aim. Control exercised kindly is still control.
invariant_mi: Disposed to do good to others; of an act or body, done or run for others' good.

domain_entries.REL: Of persons, rulers, and charitable societies.
domain_entries.COG: Of attitudes: favourable in tone, which may still restrict those they favour.
domain_entries.DIG: Of project governance: a single leader trusted to decide for the community's good.

count_condition: A party or body and an aim at others' good.
transfer_boundary: Benevolent is not beneficial or harmless. Claimed benevolence needs conduct to show it.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A spirit believed to be kindly toward people and to help or protect them.
example: Offerings were left for the benevolent spirit of the house.
rrgm_bridge: A helper whose goodwill usually depends on right relation: respect and reciprocity keep it.
invariant_mi: A spirit held by a tradition to be well-disposed toward people and to help or protect them.

domain_entries.MYT: Guardian, household, and ancestral spirits in many traditions.

count_condition: A named tradition and a spirit it describes as helpful.
transfer_boundary: Many traditions' spirits are helpful when respected and harmful when slighted, so the label can be an outsider's simplification.

common_meaning: An action done in order to benefit someone else.
example: Shovelling the neighbour's path was a small benevolent-action.
rrgm_bridge: Aimed at another's good on the actor's own initiative. It can miss, and it can run over what the recipient wanted.
invariant_mi: An act done in order to benefit another, at the actor's initiative.

domain_entries.REL: Helping, giving, and caring conduct.
domain_entries.COG: Prosocial behaviour and its motives.
domain_entries.DIG: An action by a system aimed at a user's benefit beyond what was asked.

count_condition: An act, an intended beneficiary, and evidence of the aim.
transfer_boundary: Not every beneficial act is benevolent, and not every benevolent act benefits. Where it overrides the recipient's wishes it conflicts with agency-preservation.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: At the side of; next to; compared with.
example: She sat beside the driver.
rrgm_bridge: The position of parity: neither ahead nor behind, neither above nor below.
invariant_mi: At the side of a reference, neither before, behind, above, nor below it.

domain_entries.PHY: Lateral position next to something.
domain_entries.REL: Standing with someone as a companion or equal.
domain_entries.LIN: "Beside the point": irrelevant. "Beside oneself": overcome.

count_condition: A reference and a position at its side.
transfer_boundary: Beside is not "besides", which means in addition.

common_meaning: Of the most excellent or suitable kind; to the highest degree.
example: This is the best route to the coast.
rrgm_bridge: A ranking claim. The RRGM kernel asks every comparison to be bound to a named dimension, and "best" also needs the set it was chosen from.
invariant_mi: Highest on a stated scale among the candidates considered.

domain_entries.FOR: The optimum of an objective over a set.
domain_entries.LIN: The superlative of "good" and "well".
domain_entries.ECO: Best price; best practice.
domain_entries.COG: Seeking the best, as opposed to settling for good enough.
domain_entries.DIG: "Best effort": service with no guarantee of delivery.

count_condition: A scale, a set of candidates, and the highest-ranked among them.
transfer_boundary: Best of those considered is not best possible. Best on one dimension is not best overall. "Best effort" promises effort only.

common_meaning: The most favourable outcome or conditions that could reasonably occur.
example: In the best-case scenario the bridge reopens in May.
rrgm_bridge: One end of the range. Plans built on it fail in ordinary conditions.
invariant_mi: The most favourable outcome or condition among those considered possible.

domain_entries.FOR: The least cost an algorithm can incur on any input of a given size.
domain_entries.ECO: The optimistic scenario in a forecast.
domain_entries.COG: The case people's plans tend to assume.

count_condition: A range of possible outcomes and its most favourable member.
transfer_boundary: Best-case is not expected and not guaranteed.
remainder_note: An established term, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: To be disloyal to; to harm someone who trusted one by helping their enemies or breaking a confidence.
example: He betrayed his colleagues to the police.
rrgm_bridge: Acts against reliance that was invited or owed. It presupposes a prior trust.
invariant_mi: To act against one who trusted or relied on you, in breach of that trust.

domain_entries.REL: Treason, infidelity, and breach of confidence.

invariant_mi: To reveal something unintentionally by one's behaviour or appearance.

domain_entries.COG: Involuntary signs of a concealed state.
domain_entries.DIG: Side effects such as timing or metadata that disclose what was meant to stay hidden.

common_meaning: The act of betraying someone's trust or loyalty.
example: She saw his silence as a betrayal.
rrgm_bridge: A breach by the one relied on. Calling something a betrayal is a claim that needs the trust and the act both shown.
invariant_mi: A breach of trust by one who was relied on, to the harm of the one relying.

domain_entries.REL: Between persons, and by institutions toward those who depend on them.
domain_entries.ECO: People avoid risks of being betrayed more strongly than equal risks from chance.
domain_entries.DIG: A service acting against the reliance its users placed in it.

count_condition: Prior trust or reliance, an act against it by the trusted party, and harm.
transfer_boundary: Betrayal is not disappointment, disagreement, or an open and declared departure.

common_meaning: Of a more excellent or suitable kind; improved in health; to improve on.

rrgm_bridge: A comparison that owes a dimension. The RRGM kernel asks for improvements to be accumulated and comparative debt avoided.
invariant_mi: Higher than another on a stated scale of goodness or fitness.

domain_entries.LIN: The comparative of "good" and "well"; "had better" gives advice or warning.
domain_entries.FOR: A preference ordering; an outcome is better for all when at least one gains and none loses.
domain_entries.ECO: Better off: improved in welfare.
domain_entries.BIO: Recovered or recovering.

count_condition: Two things, a scale, and a higher position for one.
transfer_boundary: Better is not good. Better for one party may be worse for another. The comparison is between outputs or options, and is no ranking of those who produced them.

common_meaning: An answer that improves on an earlier answer to the same question.

domain_entries.DIG: Selection or refinement among candidate outputs.
domain_entries.REL: Collaborative correction, in which the gain is credited to the work.

count_condition: One question, two answers, a named dimension, and a shown improvement.

common_meaning: In the space, time, or range separating two things; connecting or shared by two parties.

invariant_mi: In the interval or relation that two things bound.

common_meaning: A tendency to lean in one direction; unfair preference for or against; a systematic error.

domain_entries.REL: Partiality toward or against a person or group.

count_condition: A reference or norm, repeated cases, and a consistent direction of departure.

common_meaning: A deliberate test of whether a judgement or result leans unfairly in one direction.

invariant_mi: A deliberate test of whether a judgement or result leans systematically, made before it is relied on.

domain_entries.DIG: Substitution tests and subgroup evaluations on a system's outputs.
domain_entries.REL: Review of a decision for partiality or conflict of interest.

count_condition: A judgement, a suspected direction of lean, a test able to reveal it, and a result.

common_meaning: An adjustment made to remove or offset a known bias.

invariant_mi: An adjustment that removes or offsets a known systematic lean from a result or procedure.

domain_entries.FOR: Estimators adjusted to remove expected error.

domain_entries.COG: Techniques such as deliberately considering the opposite.

count_condition: An identified bias with direction and estimated size, an adjustment, and a check afterwards.

common_meaning: The possibility that a result is systematically wrong because of how it was produced.

domain_entries.REL: Decisions made by parties with an interest in the outcome.

common_meaning: Unfairly prejudiced; leaning systematically one way.

domain_entries.PHY: Of a junction: with a steady voltage applied.

count_condition: A source or process and a shown consistent lean.
transfer_boundary: Biased is not wrong. A biased estimator can be the better one. The word needs the lean demonstrated.

common_meaning: A list of the books and articles referred to in a work, or of works on a subject.

common_meaning: One item in a bibliography, giving the details of a single source.

invariant_mi: One record in a bibliography, identifying a single source with enough detail to locate it.

count_condition: One source, the required fields, and a format.

common_meaning: Of considerable size, extent, or importance.

common_meaning: Consisting of or involving two things; relating to the number system that uses only 0 and 1.

domain_entries.REL: A two-category classification, such as the gender binary, which some people's identities fall outside.

domain_entries.DIG: A presence flag.

common_meaning: A gate with only two outcomes: let through, or not.

domain_entries.DIG: A logic element or boolean guard.
domain_entries.FOR: A threshold function.
domain_entries.PHY: A switch with two stable positions.
domain_entries.REL: A pass-or-fail decision.

domain_entries.PHY: Discrete detection events.
domain_entries.DIG: Creation of an object or process, which either succeeds or fails.
domain_entries.FOR: A predicate satisfied or not by a candidate.

count_condition: A candidate instance, a count condition, and an outcome of instantiated or not.

common_meaning: A condition that has only two possible values, such as on and off.
example: The switch is a binary-state device.

invariant_mi: A state variable that can take exactly two values.

domain_entries.PHY: Two-level and bistable systems.
domain_entries.DIG: A boolean value or flip-flop.
domain_entries.BIO: All-or-none responses such as a nerve impulse or a cell-fate switch.

count_condition: A system and exactly two distinguishable states.
transfer_boundary: Proposed distinction: binary-state is the property of having two states; bit-state is the value a particular bit holds at a time. A quantum bit is not confined to two states before measurement.

common_meaning: To tie or fasten; to hold by obligation; to attach chemically; to associate a name with a value.
example: The contract binds both parties.
rrgm_bridge: In RRLM the active bind is the context that fixes threshold, coupling, mapping, and record conditions. A Turn is a change of bind.
invariant_mi: To fasten one thing to another so that it is held: by tie, by bond, by obligation, or by assignment.

domain_entries.PHY: To tie or stick together.
domain_entries.BIO: Of a molecule: to attach to its partner.
domain_entries.REL: To place under obligation by agreement, oath, or law.
domain_entries.FOR: To fix a variable to a value within a scope.
domain_entries.DIG: To associate a name, address, or handler with a resource.
domain_entries.LIN: To link a pronoun to its antecedent.

count_condition: Two things, a holding connection between them, and a scope in which it holds.

common_meaning: To join several things firmly into one.
example: Shared hardship bound the crew together.
rrgm_bridge: Coupling: the bound things then move and count jointly, and pulling them apart has a cost.
invariant_mi: To hold several things as one by ties among them, so that they move or count together.

domain_entries.PHY: Systems held together so that energy is needed to separate them.
domain_entries.REL: Shared obligations, rituals, and histories that hold a group.
domain_entries.COG: The combining of separate features into one perceived object.

count_condition: Several things, ties among them, and joint movement or counting.
transfer_boundary: Not aggregation, where nothing ties the members. Not fusion, where the parts lose distinctness. What binds can also confine.

common_meaning: A fastening or cover; (adjective) imposing an obligation that must be kept.

rrgm_bridge: A holding connection, or the force to hold. A binding commitment is one that has been written where it has consequences.
invariant_mi: A holding connection, or having the force to hold.

domain_entries.REL: Of an agreement, ruling, or precedent: obligatory.
domain_entries.BIO: The attachment of molecules at a specific site.
domain_entries.PHY: The energy needed to separate a bound system.
domain_entries.DIG: An interface that lets one language or system call another; an assignment of a key or name.
domain_entries.LIN: The rules linking pronouns to antecedents.

count_condition: A connection or commitment, and what it holds.

transfer_boundary: The biosphere is not an ecosystem or a biome. The hypothesis that it regulates itself is a separate claim.
