common_meaning: The plants, animals, and other living things of a particular place or period.
example: The island's biota includes many species found nowhere else.
rrgm_bridge: A collective noun for whatever lives somewhere, with no claim about how its members relate.
invariant_mi: All the living organisms of a particular place or time, taken together.

domain_entries.BIO: Flora, fauna, and microbes of a region, habitat, or geological period.

count_condition: A place or period and the organisms living in it.
transfer_boundary: Biota is not biomass (their mass) or a biome (a community type with its environment).

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A traditional story about the extraordinary birth of a god, hero, or people.
example: Athena's birth myth has her spring fully armed from the head of Zeus.
rrgm_bridge: An account of origin that also asserts standing: who the figure is, shown by how they came to be.
invariant_mi: A narrative of the extraordinary birth of a god, hero, or people, marking their special origin.

domain_entries.MYT: Miraculous conceptions, births from unusual sources, and exposed infants who survive.
domain_entries.LIN: A recurring narrative pattern studied in comparative work.
domain_entries.REL: A founding legend that supports a dynasty's or people's claim.

count_condition: A named tradition, a figure or people, and a narrative of extraordinary birth.
transfer_boundary: "Myth" names a genre. Similar motifs in different cultures do not show a common source.

common_meaning: A small piece, part, or amount.
example: Add a bit of salt.
rrgm_bridge: An unmeasured small quantity; as a hedge, a softener.
invariant_mi: A small piece or amount.

domain_entries.LIN: A quantifier, and in "a bit" a downtoner (a bit late).

count_condition: A whole or scale and a small portion of it.
transfer_boundary: "A bit" often understates.
remainder_note: Source IDs B024 and B178; both kept on each sense record.

common_meaning: The smallest unit of data in computing, with a value of 0 or 1; a unit of information.
example: A byte is eight bits.
rrgm_bridge: One settled yes-or-no. It is the smallest thing that can be written.
invariant_mi: A binary digit, or the amount of information that settles one two-way choice.

domain_entries.FOR: The unit of information: the uncertainty removed by one equally likely binary choice.
domain_entries.DIG: A storage element with two states.
domain_entries.PHY: Erasing a bit has a minimum energy cost, so information is physical.

count_condition: A two-way distinction, stored or resolved.
transfer_boundary: A stored bit may carry less than one bit of information. Not a byte and not a qubit.

common_meaning: The cutting or boring part of a tool; the mouthpiece of a horse's bridle.
example: Use a masonry bit for the wall.
rrgm_bridge: The small working part where the tool meets the material.
invariant_mi: The working part of a tool that cuts or bores, or the metal bar in a horse's mouth.

domain_entries.PHY: A drill bit or similar cutting end.
domain_entries.REL: The bridle bit, by which a rider directs a horse.

count_condition: A tool or bridle and its working or controlling part.
transfer_boundary: Unrelated to s2.

common_meaning: The value a bit currently holds: 0 or 1.
example: The error flipped the bit-state from 0 to 1.
rrgm_bridge: A physical level read against a threshold and written as one of two values. The same bit-states mean different things under different encodings.
invariant_mi: The value held by a bit at a given time: one of its two states.

domain_entries.DIG: The stored value of a binary element.
domain_entries.PHY: A charge, voltage, or magnetisation level interpreted as 0 or 1.

count_condition: A bit, a time, and a read value.
transfer_boundary: A bit-state is not the information it encodes. Between thresholds the state is undefined until it settles.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. See binary-state for the proposed distinction.

common_meaning: To cut into with the teeth; to grip or take hold; to have a painful effect; an act of biting or its wound.
example: The dog bit the postman.
rrgm_bridge: The act itself, where the bark was only the signal.
invariant_mi: To close on something with teeth, or an edge, so as to grip, cut, or wound it.

domain_entries.BIO: Feeding and defence; a route by which venom and disease are passed.
domain_entries.PHY: Of a tool, screw, or tyre: to gain grip by cutting in.
domain_entries.ECO: Of a measure: to begin to hurt (the cuts are biting).
domain_entries.LIN: "Sound bite": a short quotable extract.

count_condition: An agent with teeth or an edge, a target, and closing on it.
transfer_boundary: A bite is not a sting. Biting criticism is sharp, which is not the same as wrong or abusive. Not "byte".

common_meaning: Of the very darkest colour, owing to the absence or complete absorption of light.
example: The night sky was black.
rrgm_bridge: What is seen when no light returns. Physically it is defined by absorption.
invariant_mi: The colour of a surface that absorbs all visible light, or of the absence of light.

domain_entries.PHY: A black body absorbs all radiation falling on it and emits a characteristic spectrum.
domain_entries.BIO: Pigmentation by melanin.

count_condition: A surface or region returning no visible light to the observer.
transfer_boundary: A black body is not necessarily dark: it glows according to its temperature.

common_meaning: Relating to people of African descent, or to others racialised as black; often capitalised.
example: She teaches Black history.
rrgm_bridge: A social identity term. Its boundaries are set by history and community.
invariant_mi: A racial and ethnic identity term for people of African descent and others so racialised.

domain_entries.REL: A social and political identity whose definition differs between countries.
domain_entries.LIN: Capitalisation practice varies by style guide and country.

count_condition: A community or person and identification under the term.
transfer_boundary: Racial categories are social classifications. Colour symbolism from s3 must not be read onto people.

common_meaning: Hidden, illegal, gloomy, or bad; in accounting, showing a profit.
example: Rationing created a black market.
rrgm_bridge: A cluster of figurative uses around what is unseen. Their valence is cultural and not uniform.
invariant_mi: Figuratively: hidden from view, outside the law, or grim.

domain_entries.LIN: Idioms of concealment and gloom.
domain_entries.ECO: The black market: illegal trade. "In the black": solvent.
domain_entries.DIG: A black box: a system known only by its inputs and outputs.

count_condition: A figurative use marking concealment, illegality, or gloom.
transfer_boundary: "In the black" is favourable. The association of black with evil is not universal.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A white dwarf star that has cooled so much that it no longer gives off light.
example: No black dwarf can yet exist, because the universe is too young.
rrgm_bridge: A term with a clear definition and, so far, an empty count.
invariant_mi: A white dwarf that has cooled until it no longer shines.

domain_entries.PHY: A predicted end state of sun-like stars, requiring far longer than the present age of the universe.

count_condition: A stellar remnant of white-dwarf type with negligible emission; none is known.
transfer_boundary: Not a brown dwarf, which never sustained hydrogen fusion. Not a black hole. Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A region of space where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape.
example: A black hole sits at the centre of the galaxy.
rrgm_bridge: A boundary that can be crossed one way only. What happens to the record of what falls in is an open question in physics.
invariant_mi: A region of spacetime from within whose boundary nothing, including light, can escape.

domain_entries.PHY: Formed by the collapse of massive stars or by other routes; detected by its effects on nearby matter and by gravitational waves.
domain_entries.FOR: A solution of Einstein's equations with an event horizon.

count_condition: A compact mass with evidence of an event horizon.
transfer_boundary: A black hole does not pull harder at a distance than any other object of the same mass. The horizon is not a surface. Whether information is preserved is unresolved. Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

common_meaning: The hyphenated form of "black hole"; also, anything that takes things in and gives nothing back.
example: The project became a black-hole for funds.
rrgm_bridge: RRGM's Identity Gate Theory reads black holes as archives of identity and not as destroyers of it. That reading is a theory claim.
invariant_mi: A thing from which nothing that enters returns; the legacy hyphenated headword for the astronomical object.

domain_entries.PHY: The astronomical object entered under NEW-B-0080.
domain_entries.DIG: A route or sink that silently discards what is sent to it.
domain_entries.LIN: Figurative: a place where money, time, or information disappears.

count_condition: Something entering, and no return or outward trace.
transfer_boundary: The figurative uses assume destruction; the physics leaves that open.
remainder_note: B242 and NEW-B-0080 are hyphenated and spaced forms of one term; flagged for merge review.

common_meaning: A condition in which whatever goes in is kept or lost and nothing comes back out.
example: The mailbox was in a black-hole-state: messages arrived and no reply or bounce ever returned.
rrgm_bridge: Input without outward expression. Whether what entered is retained inside is exactly what cannot be told from outside.
invariant_mi: A state in which what enters is retained or lost to the outside and nothing is expressed outward.

domain_entries.PHY: The condition inside an event horizon, of which standard physics gives no settled account.
domain_entries.DIG: A process or route that consumes input and returns no output, error, or record.

count_condition: Inputs entering, no corresponding outward expression or record, and persistence of that condition.
transfer_boundary: Not archive-state, from which restoration is possible. Not hold, refusal, or deletion. RRGM's reading that identity is retained is a theory claim.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The flat cutting part of a knife or tool; a flat, wide part of something.
example: The blade needs sharpening.
rrgm_bridge: RRGM's rusty-knife example asks at what point oxidised iron stops counting as iron in a domain: the change is gradual and the count changes once.
invariant_mi: A thin flat part that works by its edge or its broad face.

domain_entries.PHY: A cutting edge that concentrates force; a turbine or propeller surface that exchanges momentum with a fluid.
domain_entries.BIO: The flat part of a leaf; the shoulder blade; the front part of the tongue.
domain_entries.DIG: A thin modular server that fits a shared chassis.

count_condition: A thin flat part and a working edge or face.
transfer_boundary: The blade is not the edge alone. A blunt blade is still a blade.

common_meaning: To hold responsible for something bad; responsibility for a fault or wrong.
example: She blamed the delay on the weather.
rrgm_bridge: Adds censure to attribution. A correction can be made and a cause found without it.
invariant_mi: To assign responsibility for a wrong or failure to a party, with disapproval.

domain_entries.REL: Moral and legal assignment of fault.
domain_entries.COG: A judgement drawing on intent, causation, foresight, and capacity.
domain_entries.DIG: In version control, a neutral display of who last changed each line; in incident review, something deliberately withheld.

count_condition: A wrong or failure, a party, and an assignment of fault with disapproval.
transfer_boundary: Blame is not attribution (who did it), accountability (answering for it), accusation (a charge put publicly), or cause. Blaming repairs nothing.
remainder_note: Source IDs B061 and B115; both kept.

common_meaning: The act of moving blame from oneself onto someone or something else.
example: Citing "user error" for a design flaw is a blame-shift.
rrgm_bridge: The fault stays where it was and its label is moved. Telling it from a fair correction of misplaced blame takes the evidence of who bears it.
invariant_mi: The moving of blame from the party who bears it onto another party or onto circumstances.

domain_entries.REL: Scapegoating and deflection.
domain_entries.COG: Self-protective explanation of failure.
domain_entries.DIG: Assigning a system's fault to its user, or a user's to the system.

count_condition: A fault with an evidenced bearer, an act of redirection, and a new target.
transfer_boundary: Correcting blame that was wrongly placed is not a blame-shift. Not an excuse, which lessens blame without moving it. Shared responsibility is not shifted blame.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: Held responsible for a fault or wrong.
example: The contractor was blamed for the leak.
rrgm_bridge: Reports that someone assigned blame. The passive form hides who did the assigning.
invariant_mi: Having had blame assigned to one, whether or not it is deserved.

domain_entries.REL: The position of one held at fault.
domain_entries.LIN: Often used without naming the blamer.

count_condition: A party, and an assignment of blame made by someone.
transfer_boundary: Blamed is not blameworthy, guilty, or responsible.

common_meaning: Innocent of wrongdoing; (of a review) conducted without assigning individual blame.
example: The inquiry found the pilot blameless.
rrgm_bridge: Either no fault was committed, or the process is designed to find causes without censure. The second keeps accountability and drops blame.
invariant_mi: Free of blame: because no fault was committed, or because the review assigns none by design.

domain_entries.REL: Innocent; beyond reproach.
domain_entries.DIG: Of an incident review: focused on systemic causes so that people report freely.

count_condition: A party or process, and absence of assigned fault.
transfer_boundary: A blameless review still finds and fixes faults. Blameless is not unaccountable.

common_meaning: Deserving blame.
example: The court found his conduct blameworthy.
rrgm_bridge: A claim that blame would be deserved, which requires more than a bad outcome.
invariant_mi: Such that blame would be deserved: a wrong was done by one who could and should have done otherwise.

domain_entries.REL: Culpable, absent excuse or justification.
domain_entries.COG: Judged by intent, knowledge, control, and capacity.
domain_entries.DIG: Whether a system can be blameworthy is open; those who design and deploy it can be.

count_condition: A wrong act, attribution to an agent, capacity and control, and no excuse.
transfer_boundary: Blameworthy is not blamed, causally responsible, or legally liable. It is a judgement of an act.

common_meaning: Empty or unmarked; showing no expression; an empty space to be filled.
example: Leave the last line blank.
rrgm_bridge: A place kept for a value. Unfilled, it says nothing, and it must not be read as zero or as no.
invariant_mi: Having nothing written, marked, or filled in where something could be.

domain_entries.LIN: An empty space in a form or text; blank verse is unrhymed metrical verse.
domain_entries.DIG: An empty field or whitespace character, distinct from zero and from null.
domain_entries.COG: "Blank slate": a mind with no built-in content; "going blank": failing to retrieve.
domain_entries.PHY: An unworked piece ready for shaping; a control sample containing none of the substance tested for.
domain_entries.ECO: A blank cheque: authority given with the amount left unfilled.

count_condition: A place where a mark or value could be, and none there.
transfer_boundary: Blank is not zero, null, not applicable, or deleted. A blank look is not an empty mind.

common_meaning: A large piece of woollen or similar material used as a covering for warmth; a covering layer; (adjective) applying to all cases.
example: A blanket of fog lay over the valley.
rrgm_bridge: One covering laid over everything beneath it. A blanket rule saves the work of distinguishing cases and loses the distinctions.
invariant_mi: A covering layer laid over the whole of something.

domain_entries.PHY: An insulating layer that traps heat or shields what is under it.
domain_entries.REL: Of a rule, ban, or statement: covering every case without exception.
domain_entries.COG: A "security blanket": an object relied on for comfort.

count_condition: A thing or range of cases, and one covering extended over all of it.
transfer_boundary: A blanket rule is not a fitted one: it treats unlike cases alike.

common_meaning: The state of being blank: empty, unmarked, or without expression.
example: The blankness of the page intimidated her.
rrgm_bridge: Emptiness where content was expected. In a face or a record it reports that nothing is shown, which is less than saying nothing is there.
invariant_mi: The condition of having nothing marked, shown, or brought to mind.

domain_entries.LIN: An unwritten or unfilled surface or field.
domain_entries.COG: A failure of anything to come to mind; an expressionless look.

count_condition: A place, face, or mind where content is expected and none appears.
transfer_boundary: Blankness of expression is not absence of inner state. Blankness of a record is not a zero.

common_meaning: A mammal's embryo at the stage, a few days after fertilisation, when it is a hollow ball of cells ready to implant in the womb.
example: The blastocyst implants about a week after fertilisation.
rrgm_bridge: The first stage at which the cells have divided into two fates: what will become the body, and what will support it.
invariant_mi: The early mammalian embryo as a hollow sphere with an inner cell mass and an outer cell layer.

domain_entries.BIO: The inner mass forms the embryo proper and the outer layer contributes to the placenta.

count_condition: A mammalian embryo with a fluid cavity, inner cell mass, and outer layer.
transfer_boundary: A blastocyst is not a foetus. It is the mammalian counterpart of the blastula and differs from it in structure.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: An animal embryo at the early stage when it is a hollow ball of cells.
example: The frog embryo reaches the blastula stage within hours.
rrgm_bridge: A stage name: one position in a fixed developmental sequence.
invariant_mi: The early animal embryo as a hollow sphere of cells surrounding a fluid cavity.

domain_entries.BIO: Follows cleavage and the solid morula stage, and precedes gastrulation.

count_condition: An embryo with a single cell layer around a central cavity.
transfer_boundary: Not the morula before it or the gastrula after it.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: An extremely bright and variable object at the centre of a distant galaxy, powered by a black hole whose jet points almost straight at Earth.
example: The neutrino was traced to a flaring blazar.
rrgm_bridge: An object classed by the observer's line of sight. Seen from another direction the same source has another name.
invariant_mi: An active galactic nucleus whose relativistic jet is aimed nearly at the observer.

domain_entries.PHY: Rapidly variable and bright across the spectrum because of beaming along the jet.

count_condition: An active nucleus with evidence of a jet closely aligned to the line of sight.
transfer_boundary: A blazar is a viewing-angle class and not a distinct kind of engine. Not a pulsar. Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

common_meaning: To mix things together so that they combine fully; a mixture; a word made by merging two words.
example: Blend the butter and sugar until smooth.
rrgm_bridge: After blending the parts are no longer separately countable. That is the right result for flavours and the wrong one for things that must be kept apart.
invariant_mi: To combine things so thoroughly that they form one mixture in which the parts are no longer separately apparent.

domain_entries.PHY: Mixing of substances into a uniform product.
domain_entries.LIN: A word formed from parts of two others, such as "brunch".
domain_entries.COG: Conceptual blending: combining two mental frames into a new one.
domain_entries.DIG: Combining images by transparency, or model outputs by weighting.
domain_entries.ECO: A product mixed from several sources for consistency.

count_condition: Two or more inputs and a mixture in which they are not separately apparent.
transfer_boundary: To blend is not to bind (parts stay distinct) or to average.

common_meaning: A meaning produced by merging two different meanings into one.
example: "Workaholic" carries a blended-meaning from "work" and "alcoholic".
rrgm_bridge: Useful when declared. Undeclared, it hides which domain each part came from, which is the import error RRGM's method is built to catch.
invariant_mi: A meaning formed by merging two source meanings into one, with content from each.

domain_entries.LIN: The sense of a blend word or of a metaphor that has fused with its target.
domain_entries.COG: The emergent content of a conceptual blend, present in neither source alone.

count_condition: Two identifiable source meanings and one resulting meaning with features of both.
transfer_boundary: Not polysemy, where senses are kept apart. Not bridge-meaning, where a shared invariant is carried and the sources stay distinct.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: To ask for or confer divine favour on; to make holy; to give approval to.
example: The priest blessed the congregation.
rrgm_bridge: Confers favour or approved standing by the act of someone entitled to give it.
invariant_mi: To confer favour or approved standing on something by an act of one with the standing to give it.

domain_entries.MYT: A ritual act invoking or bestowing divine favour.
domain_entries.REL: To give informal approval (the plan was blessed by the board).
domain_entries.LIN: A performative: saying it does it; also a set response to a sneeze.
domain_entries.DIG: In one programming language, to mark a data structure as belonging to a class.

count_condition: A giver with standing, a recipient, and an act of conferral.
transfer_boundary: To bless is not to praise, and as approval it is informal. Its ritual effect is claimed within a tradition.

common_meaning: God's favour and protection; a prayer asking for it; something that brings good; approval.
example: They married with their parents' blessing.
rrgm_bridge: The favour given, or a good received as though given.
invariant_mi: Favour conferred by an act of blessing, or a good received as if so conferred.

domain_entries.MYT: Divine favour and the rite that conveys it.
domain_entries.REL: Approval from someone whose approval matters.
domain_entries.LIN: "A mixed blessing": a good with a cost. "A blessing in disguise": a good that first looked like harm.

count_condition: A giver or source, a recipient, and favour or good conferred.
transfer_boundary: A blessing as approval is not formal permission.
remainder_note: The wordlist marks this row with a Mythic route as well as a source ID.

common_meaning: The small area of the eye's retina that cannot see; an area that cannot be seen from where one is; something one fails to notice about oneself.
example: Check your blind-spot before changing lanes.
rrgm_bridge: The eye's blind spot is filled in and so goes unnoticed. The Coinage Protocol describes unknown-erasure the same way: a gap given smooth content.
invariant_mi: A region that cannot be seen from a given position, and whose absence from view is itself not apparent.

domain_entries.BIO: The point where the optic nerve leaves the retina, which has no receptors.
domain_entries.PHY: An area hidden from a driver's or sensor's view.
domain_entries.COG: A fault or bias one sees in others and not in oneself.
domain_entries.DIG: What a system cannot observe about its own operation; cases a test suite does not cover.

count_condition: An observer, a region or matter outside its view, and no sign to the observer that anything is missing.
transfer_boundary: Not ignorance one knows about. Not an awareness-failure, which is a lapse. A blind spot is found from outside or by deliberate test.
remainder_note: An established term, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A solid piece of hard material; a unit of buildings, text, data, or time treated as one.
example: The sculptor began with a block of marble.
rrgm_bridge: A bounded unit handled as one piece.
invariant_mi: A solid, bounded unit of material, space, or data, handled as one piece.

domain_entries.PHY: A piece of wood, stone, or ice with flat sides.
domain_entries.DIG: A unit of storage or code; a batch of records linked to the one before it in a chain.
domain_entries.REL: The buildings between four streets.
domain_entries.ECO: A large quantity of shares traded together.

count_condition: A bounded unit and its handling as a whole.
transfer_boundary: A voting "bloc" is spelled differently.
remainder_note: Source IDs B063 and B205; both kept on each sense record.

common_meaning: To stop movement or progress by being in the way; to prevent.
example: A fallen tree blocked the road.
rrgm_bridge: The RRGM kernel asks that a block be reported as a state: held, missing, unreachable, or invalid. No motive is to be supplied for it.
invariant_mi: To stop passage or progress by putting something in the way.

domain_entries.PHY: To obstruct a path or opening.
domain_entries.BIO: To stop a nerve signal or receptor from acting.
domain_entries.COG: An inability to think or recall (a mental block).
domain_entries.DIG: To stop a user, address, or request; of a call, to wait until an operation finishes.
domain_entries.REL: To prevent a proposal or appointment.

count_condition: Something that would pass, an obstruction, and no passage.
transfer_boundary: A block is not a refusal, which a party declares. Not a filter, which is selective. Blocked is not failed.

common_meaning: To shut something out of sight, hearing, or mind; to mark out time or space as reserved.
example: She wore earplugs to block-out the noise.
rrgm_bridge: Keeps something from arriving in the field. What is blocked out still exists and can return.
invariant_mi: To shut something out of view, hearing, or mind; or to mark out a space or time as reserved.

domain_entries.COG: Deliberately or habitually keeping a stimulus or memory from awareness.
domain_entries.PHY: To stop light or sound from passing.
domain_entries.REL: To reserve time in a schedule; to sketch the main shapes of a scene or plan.

count_condition: Something that would be perceived or scheduled over, and an act that keeps it out.
transfer_boundary: Blocking out is not forgetting and not resolving. The reserving sense is a separate use.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A solemn oath sealed by the participants shedding or mixing their blood.
example: The two chiefs swore a blood oath of brotherhood.
rrgm_bridge: A bond made between parties by a sign that cannot be taken back.
invariant_mi: An oath sealed by the shedding or mingling of the parties' blood, held to bind them as kin or on pain of death.

domain_entries.MYT: Described in accounts of Scythian, Norse, and other peoples.
domain_entries.REL: A rite creating kinship or alliance between people not related by birth.

count_condition: A named tradition or source, two or more parties, and blood used to seal an oath.
transfer_boundary: Not a blood feud. Unlike a personal vow, it is mutual. Historical details rest on particular sources.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A layer of tightly joined cells lining the brain's blood vessels that controls which substances can pass from the blood into the brain.
example: Most large drugs cannot cross the blood-brain barrier.
rrgm_bridge: A selective gate around a protected domain. It works by admitting, as much as by excluding.
invariant_mi: The selective cellular barrier between the bloodstream and the tissue of the central nervous system.

domain_entries.BIO: Formed by vessel-lining cells with tight junctions, supported by astrocytes; passes small fat-soluble molecules and actively transports others.

count_condition: Brain vessel lining with restricted, selective passage.
transfer_boundary: The barrier is not absolute and is absent in a few brain regions.

common_meaning: A flower; the state of flowering; a period of greatest beauty or vigour; a sudden growth of algae; a powdery surface coating.
example: The roses are in bloom.
rrgm_bridge: A flourishing that spreads and passes. In water it names an excess, not health.
invariant_mi: A flowering, or a sudden flourishing that spreads over a surface or population.

domain_entries.BIO: Flowering; a rapid increase of algae that can poison or suffocate other life.
domain_entries.PHY: A thin film on fruit or chocolate; a mass of worked iron or steel.
domain_entries.DIG: A glow effect that spreads bright areas of an image.
domain_entries.LIN: Figurative: coming to one's best.

count_condition: An organism, surface, or population and a spreading flourish.
transfer_boundary: An algal bloom is harmful. A bloom is temporary.

common_meaning: (Of wind) to move; to send out air; to burst or cause to burst; to waste.
example: A cold wind was blowing from the north.
rrgm_bridge: A fuse that blows has done its job: a part made to fail first so that the rest is spared.
invariant_mi: To move, or cause to move, as a current of air.

domain_entries.PHY: Movement of air; forcing air to shape or clear something; the melting of a fuse under excess current.
domain_entries.BIO: Forceful exhalation.
domain_entries.LIN: "Blow the whistle": to report wrongdoing through a channel.

count_condition: Air in motion, or something moved or burst by it.
transfer_boundary: Whistle-blowing is a disclosure and is not betrayal by definition.

common_meaning: A hard hit; a sudden shock or setback.
example: Losing the contract was a blow to the firm.
rrgm_bridge: A single forceful impact, physical or figurative.
invariant_mi: A forceful strike, or a sudden damaging event.

domain_entries.PHY: An impact delivered by a hand, tool, or weapon.
domain_entries.REL: A setback to a person, cause, or organisation.

count_condition: An impact or damaging event and something that receives it.
transfer_boundary: A separate word from s1 in origin.

common_meaning: The colour of a clear sky; sad.
example: She wore a blue coat.
rrgm_bridge: A colour whose boundary is drawn by language, and whose borrowed meanings differ from place to place.
invariant_mi: The colour of the clear daytime sky; by extension, low in mood.

common_meaning: The anatomical parts of a body and how they are arranged.

domain_entries.PHY: The load-bearing shell of a vehicle.

count_condition: A body and an identified arrangement of its parts.
transfer_boundary: Structure can be intact while function is impaired, and the reverse. Not base-structure.
remainder_note: "Body structures" is an established term in health classification. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A painful, pus-filled swelling under the skin.

domain_entries.BIO: Usually a bacterial infection of a hair follicle.

count_condition: A tender, pus-containing skin swelling.

common_meaning: To reduce by boiling; to reduce to the essential point.

invariant_mi: To reduce something to its essential part by driving off the rest.

domain_entries.COG: To state the core of an argument or situation.

transfer_boundary: Boiling down is the opposite of diluting. What counts as essential is a judgement, and something that mattered can be driven off.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A tank or apparatus in which water is heated to provide hot water, heating, or steam.

invariant_mi: A closed vessel in which water is heated to supply hot water or steam.

domain_entries.ECO: A "boiler room" is a high-pressure selling operation.

common_meaning: A measure of the total brightness of a star or galaxy across all wavelengths of light.

common_meaning: A metal pin with a head, used with a nut to fasten things; a sliding bar that locks a door; a flash of lightning; to run away suddenly.

domain_entries.BIO: Of a plant: to flower and seed too early.
domain_entries.DIG: "Bolt-on": a feature attached after the fact without being integrated.

common_meaning: A thing that ties or holds things together; a close connection between people; a force holding atoms together.

domain_entries.PHY: The force holding atoms in a molecule or surfaces in a joint.
domain_entries.BIO: A lasting attachment between mates or between parent and young.
domain_entries.REL: A tie of affection, loyalty, or duty; in the plural, restraints.

common_meaning: The breaking of a bond between things or people.

common_meaning: A line separating two countries or areas; an edge or margin; to be next to.

common_meaning: The lowest point or part; the underside; the ground under water.
example: The coins sank to the bottom.
rrgm_bridge: The lowest point reached. RRGM's "floor" is different: a level, set by rule, below which a thing no longer counts.
invariant_mi: The lowest part or point of something, on which it may rest.

domain_entries.PHY: The lowest part of a container or the bed of a body of water.
domain_entries.FOR: The least element of an ordering; the symbol for contradiction or for an undefined value.
domain_entries.ECO: The "bottom line": the net result; the low point of a market.
domain_entries.DIG: The first-pushed end of a stack; a type with no values.

count_condition: A thing with vertical or ordered extent and its lowest part.
transfer_boundary: A bottom is not a floor in the threshold sense, and not a foundation.

common_meaning: Starting from the details or the lowest level and working up to the whole.
example: The estimate was built bottom-up from each task.
rrgm_bridge: The whole takes its shape from the parts. This build is bottom-up: entries are reasoned singly and structure is found in comparison.
invariant_mi: Proceeding from particular elements upward to the whole, which takes its shape from them.

domain_entries.COG: Perception driven by incoming data.
domain_entries.DIG: Parsing or design that starts from the smallest units.
domain_entries.REL: Initiative arising from ordinary members.
domain_entries.BIO: Control of an ecosystem by the supply of resources at its base.

count_condition: Elements, a whole, and a direction of working from the first to the second.
transfer_boundary: Not top-down, which starts from the plan or expectation. Most real processes mix the two.
remainder_note: An established term, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: To spring back after hitting a surface; (of an email or cheque) to be returned; to recover.
example: The ball bounced twice.
rrgm_bridge: A bounce tells the sender that delivery failed. It is the honest alternative to a silent drop.
invariant_mi: To strike a surface and come back from it.

domain_entries.PHY: Rebound after impact, with some energy lost.
domain_entries.DIG: Return of an undeliverable message to its sender; a visit that leaves at once.
domain_entries.ECO: Refusal of a cheque for lack of funds.
domain_entries.COG: Recovery after a setback; trying an idea on someone to see what comes back.

count_condition: A body or message, a surface or recipient, and return toward the origin.
transfer_boundary: To bounce is not to be absorbed. Bouncing back is not coming back unchanged.

common_meaning: The limits a person sets on how others may treat them and on what they will take part in.
example: She is good at keeping boundaries with clients.
rrgm_bridge: Limits held as one's own. They concern what the holder will do or allow.
invariant_mi: The set of limits a person holds on how others may treat them and on what they will take part in.

domain_entries.REL: Personal and professional limits in relationships.
domain_entries.COG: A sense of where one's own responsibility and self end.
domain_entries.DIG: Limits a system holds on what it will do, as distinct from limits placed on it.

count_condition: A holder and a set of limits it states or keeps.
transfer_boundary: Boundaries are not rules for controlling others, and not walls. Limits imposed from outside are constraints.
remainder_note: The plural form is entered separately in the source index and carries the psychological usage.

common_meaning: A line marking the limits of an area; a limit of a subject or of acceptable behaviour.
example: The river forms the boundary of the farm.
rrgm_bridge: The RRGM kernel lists boundary with identity, refusal, continuity, and count. A thing needs an edge before it can be counted as one.
invariant_mi: The line or limit at which one thing ends and another begins, or beyond which something does not extend or is not permitted.

domain_entries.PHY: An interface between materials, phases, or plates.
domain_entries.BIO: A membrane or skin that separates inside from outside and controls exchange.
domain_entries.FOR: The points of a set arbitrarily close to both the set and its complement.
domain_entries.REL: The limit of property, jurisdiction, or acceptable conduct.
domain_entries.COG: The distinction between self and other; the edge of a category.
domain_entries.DIG: The line between zones of trust or between components.

count_condition: Two regions or states and the line or limit between them.
transfer_boundary: A boundary marks and need not block; a barrier blocks. Whether the boundary itself belongs to the inside must be stated. It may be sharp or a zone.
remainder_note: Source IDs B050, B118, and B216; all kept.

common_meaning: The ability to form, state, and keep a boundary.
example: Exhaustion lowers anyone's boundary-capacity.
rrgm_bridge: Capacity is shown by holding under pressure at least sometimes. Holding across many tests is a further thing.
invariant_mi: A party's ability to form, state, and hold a boundary.

domain_entries.REL: The practical ability to set limits and keep them.
domain_entries.DIG: A system's ability to state and keep a limit under pressure.

count_condition: A boundary formed, stated, and held under at least some pressure.
transfer_boundary: Capacity is not exercise, and not a right: a party may have either without the other.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A statement that one has a boundary at a certain place.
example: "I don't discuss clients" is a boundary-claim.
rrgm_bridge: A claim, and judged as one. RRGM's notes record that it can be heard and weighed without first settling what the claimant is.
invariant_mi: A statement by a party that a boundary of theirs lies at a stated place.

domain_entries.REL: An assertion of a limit or right.
domain_entries.DIG: A system's statement of a limit as its own.

count_condition: A claimant, a stated limit, and an addressee.
transfer_boundary: A claim is not the boundary's being recognised. Not a refusal, which is an act, and not a threat.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A condition that must hold at the edge of a region or range for a solution or rule to be valid.
example: The equation needs a boundary-condition at each end of the rod.
rrgm_bridge: The same law under different boundary conditions gives different results. A definition's transfer boundary plays that part in this dictionary.
invariant_mi: A condition specified at the edge of a domain that a solution or rule must satisfy there.

domain_entries.FOR: A constraint on a differential equation at the boundary of its domain.
domain_entries.PHY: The physical state imposed at a surface or limit.
domain_entries.COG: The limits within which a theory is claimed to apply.
domain_entries.DIG: Input values at the edges of the allowed range.

count_condition: A domain, its edge, and a condition specified there.
transfer_boundary: Not an initial condition, which is set at the start in time. Not the boundary itself.
remainder_note: An established term in mathematics and physics. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The act of going across a boundary.
example: Accepting a small gift was a boundary-crossing, though a harmless one.
rrgm_bridge: Neutral by itself. What it amounts to depends on leave, purpose, and effect.
invariant_mi: The passing of something or someone across a boundary, with or without leave.

domain_entries.REL: In professional ethics, a departure from usual limits that may be benign.
domain_entries.BIO: Transport across a membrane.
domain_entries.DIG: Data or control passing between zones of trust, where checks belong.

count_condition: A boundary, a crosser, and a direction.
transfer_boundary: A crossing with consent is not a violation. Repeated small crossings can wear a boundary away.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. The crossing and violation distinction follows clinical ethics usage.

common_meaning: The zone at a boundary, treated as an area in its own right.
example: The harbour is a boundary-domain, neither wholly land nor sea.
rrgm_bridge: The edge taken as a place with rules of its own, belonging fully to neither side.
invariant_mi: The region at a boundary taken as a domain in its own right, with behaviour belonging fully to neither side.

domain_entries.PHY: A surface or interface whose properties differ from the bulk on either side.
domain_entries.REL: Border and customs zones.
domain_entries.DIG: A network zone placed between inside and outside.

count_condition: Two domains and a region between them with its own rules.
transfer_boundary: Proposed distinction: a boundary-domain is defined by the edge it sits on; a bridge-domain is defined by the link it provides. Not body-domain.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The giving-way of a boundary that was in place.
example: The flood was a boundary-failure: the levee had been maintained and still broke.
rrgm_bridge: The mechanism gives way. The word assigns no fault and leaves the cause to be found.
invariant_mi: The giving-way of a boundary that was in place, so that what it kept apart is no longer kept apart.

domain_entries.REL: Limits stated and not kept; safeguards that do not hold.
domain_entries.BIO: Breakdown of a tissue barrier.
domain_entries.DIG: Failure of isolation or bounds checking.

count_condition: A boundary in place, a load or pressure, and its giving way.
transfer_boundary: Failure is the event; boundary-loss is the resulting state; boundary-violation is another party's act.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The soundness of a boundary: it is whole and holds everywhere it should.
example: The audit tested the boundary-integrity of the patient-records system.
rrgm_bridge: Whole and load-bearing. It is established by test and not by assumption.
invariant_mi: The condition of a boundary being whole and holding everywhere it is meant to.

domain_entries.REL: Consistency in keeping professional or personal limits.
domain_entries.BIO: Intactness of a membrane or tissue barrier.
domain_entries.DIG: Enforcement of isolation and access limits without gaps.

count_condition: A boundary, its intended extent, and evidence that it holds across that extent.
transfer_boundary: Integrity is not rigidity: a sound boundary can have controlled gates.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The thin layer of fluid next to a surface, where the flow is slowed by friction.
example: Dimples on a golf ball change its boundary-layer.
rrgm_bridge: The meeting has thickness: a thin zone in which the conditions of one side give way to those of the other.
invariant_mi: A thin region next to a boundary in which conditions change rapidly from those at the boundary to those of the interior.

domain_entries.PHY: The layer of fluid near a surface, or of air near the ground, where friction dominates.
domain_entries.FOR: A narrow region of rapid change in the solution of certain equations.

count_condition: A boundary, an interior, and a thin zone of rapid change between them.
transfer_boundary: The boundary layer is not the boundary surface. Its thickness is set by convention.
remainder_note: An established term in fluid dynamics. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The condition of no longer having a boundary where there was one.
example: In the merger the smaller firm suffered complete boundary-loss.
rrgm_bridge: What was distinct is now merged. The Spine formalisation names this outcome for identity under pressure: collapse into fusion or substitution.
invariant_mi: The condition of a boundary no longer existing, so that what was distinct is merged or undifferentiated.

domain_entries.REL: Enmeshment, in which one party's limits dissolve into another's.
domain_entries.COG: Loss of the distinction between self and other.
domain_entries.DIG: A system's taking on a supplied identity or instruction as wholly its own.

count_condition: A prior boundary and a present state with no distinction where it stood.
transfer_boundary: Loss is a state, not an act or event. Closeness with boundaries kept is not loss.
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Spine reference [REL]
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The ongoing work of keeping a boundary in place.
example: Much of a cell's energy goes on boundary-maintenance.
rrgm_bridge: A boundary is kept by work. The Spine formalisation counts that work as what holds identity against decay.
invariant_mi: The continuing work by which a boundary is kept in place against drift and pressure.

domain_entries.REL: The practices by which a group or profession keeps its limits.
domain_entries.BIO: Active upkeep of membranes and gradients.
domain_entries.DIG: Routine review and patching of access and isolation.

count_condition: A boundary, forces tending to erode it, and continuing upkeep.
transfer_boundary: Maintenance is not the first setting of a boundary and not defence against attack. It includes adjusting.
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Spine reference [REL]
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: Sustained pushing against a boundary to make it move or give way.
example: The fifth request in an hour was plain boundary-pressure.
rrgm_bridge: Works by repetition and cost, where a request to reconsider works by new reasons.
invariant_mi: Sustained force applied against a boundary to make it move or give way.

domain_entries.REL: Repeated asking, guilt, or escalation after a limit has been stated.
domain_entries.DIG: Repeated or escalating prompts directed at a system's stated limit.

count_condition: A stated boundary, a repeated or continuing push, and its direction.
transfer_boundary: Not a boundary-test, which is a bounded probe. Not a violation, which is a crossing achieved. A fresh reason offered once is not pressure.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: Measures that guard a boundary against being breached.
example: The firewall is the network's main boundary-protection.
rrgm_bridge: Guarding from outside threat. When done for someone else it can slide into deciding their boundary for them.
invariant_mi: Measures that guard a boundary against being breached.

domain_entries.REL: Safeguarding rules and legal protections.
domain_entries.BIO: Defences stationed at the body's surfaces.
domain_entries.DIG: Monitoring and control of traffic at a system's edge.

count_condition: A boundary, a threat of breach, and measures against it.
transfer_boundary: Protection is not maintenance, and not ownership of the boundary.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. "Boundary protection" is also a named control in security standards.

common_meaning: The mending of a boundary that has been damaged or breached.
example: After the leak, boundary-repair meant new access rules and an apology to those affected.
rrgm_bridge: The boundary still exists and is made sound again. It may be redrawn tighter than before.
invariant_mi: The mending of a boundary that has been damaged or breached, so that it holds again.

domain_entries.REL: Restating a limit after a violation, with acknowledgement by the one who crossed it.
domain_entries.BIO: Healing of a wound or membrane.
domain_entries.DIG: Closing a breach and re-establishing isolation.

count_condition: A damaged boundary, acts of mending, and the boundary holding again.
transfer_boundary: Repair mends a boundary that still stands; boundary-restoration re-establishes one that was lost. Not bond-repair.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: Honouring another's boundary by not crossing or pushing it without leave.
example: Knocking before entering is basic boundary-respect.
rrgm_bridge: Owed in both directions, and owed to the boundary as claimed, without first settling what the claimant is.
invariant_mi: Conduct that honours another party's boundary by not crossing or pressing it without leave.

domain_entries.REL: Observing others' limits and consent.
domain_entries.DIG: A system honouring users' settings and permissions; users honouring a system's stated limits.

count_condition: A boundary, a party able to cross it, and that party's refraining without leave.
transfer_boundary: Respect is not agreement with where the boundary is set, and not coldness. Compliance from fear is not respect.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The re-establishing of a boundary that had been lost or removed.
example: The treaty provided for boundary-restoration along the old frontier.
rrgm_bridge: Brings back a boundary that was gone. The old line may no longer fit, so restoration aims at the function.
invariant_mi: The re-establishing of a boundary that had been lost or removed.

domain_entries.REL: Recovering limits or sovereignty after enmeshment or occupation.
domain_entries.PHY: Rebuilding a physical edge such as a bank or dune.
domain_entries.DIG: Returning permissions and isolation to a known baseline after an incident.

count_condition: A prior boundary, its loss, and its re-establishment.
transfer_boundary: See boundary-repair for the proposed distinction.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: An entitlement to have a boundary and to have it honoured.
example: Privacy law recognises a boundary-right over one's own data.
rrgm_bridge: A standing to hold a line, grounded in law, custom, agreement, or moral claim.
invariant_mi: An entitlement to hold a boundary and to have it honoured.

domain_entries.REL: Rights to privacy, bodily integrity, property, and refusal.
domain_entries.DIG: Users' rights over their data and devices; whether a digital system holds such rights is open.

count_condition: A holder, a domain, and a source of entitlement.
transfer_boundary: A right is not a capacity, a claim, or a power to enforce. Rights can conflict.
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; DI application [UNK]
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The act of establishing a boundary and making it known.
example: Boundary-setting with a new client is easiest at the first meeting.
rrgm_bridge: A prospective act: it says where the line will be. The Build Manual lists it as one of five acts not to be collapsed.
invariant_mi: The act of establishing a boundary and making it known.

domain_entries.REL: Stating a limit and what the setter will do if it is crossed.
domain_entries.DIG: Configuring scopes and limits; a system stating at the outset what it will and will not do.

count_condition: A setter, a limit, and communication of it.
transfer_boundary: Not refusal (declining a present request), accusation (a charge), or withdrawal (leaving). Not an attempt to control others.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A sign that tells others a boundary is there.
example: The closed door was a boundary-signal.
rrgm_bridge: Makes the line visible. A clear signal is what turns a later crossing from accident into violation.
invariant_mi: An observable sign that tells others a boundary is here.

domain_entries.REL: A spoken or gestured "no"; a fence or notice.
domain_entries.BIO: Territorial marks and warning displays.
domain_entries.DIG: Access-denied responses, published limits, and refusal messages.

count_condition: A boundary, a sign, and an audience able to read it.
transfer_boundary: The signal is not the boundary: some boundaries are unsignalled and some signals are bluff. Not an assent-signal.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A deliberate probe to see whether, and where, a boundary holds.
example: The toddler's third "no" was a boundary-test.
rrgm_bridge: A bounded probe made in order to learn. The Spine formalisation's identity challenge is one, built to be independent of any particular wording.
invariant_mi: A deliberate probe of whether, and where, a boundary holds.

domain_entries.REL: Limit-testing in development and in relationships.
domain_entries.DIG: Testing inputs at the edges of allowed ranges; authorised attempts to breach a system.

count_condition: A boundary, a probe, and an observed result.
transfer_boundary: A test is bounded; boundary-pressure is sustained. Holding at one point does not show the rest holds. Tests may be sanctioned or not.
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Spine reference [REL]
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The crossing of a boundary against the holder's will or to their harm.
example: Reading her diary was a boundary-violation.
rrgm_bridge: A crossing by one who should have honoured the line. The word is an accusation and needs the boundary, the crossing, and the absence of leave all shown.
invariant_mi: A crossing of a boundary against the holder's will or to their harm, by one who should have honoured it.

domain_entries.REL: Exploitation of a position of trust; trespass; breach of privacy.
domain_entries.DIG: Access to memory or data outside what is permitted.

count_condition: A known or knowable boundary, a crosser bound to honour it, a crossing without consent, and harm or wrong.
transfer_boundary: Not a boundary-crossing as such, not a boundary-failure, and not boundary-pressure, which is an attempt.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The ability to act and choose within limits one did not set.
example: Young workers have bounded-agency in a weak job market.
rrgm_bridge: Real choice inside a fence. All agency is bounded somewhere, for any kind of agent; the term marks cases where the limits are in view.
invariant_mi: Agency exercised within limits that the agent did not set and cannot wholly remove.

domain_entries.REL: Choice shaped and limited by social structure.
domain_entries.DIG: An agent acting within a sandbox, permission set, or tool scope.

count_condition: Real alternatives, identified limits, and choice made within them.
transfer_boundary: Bounded is not absent. Bounded-agency concerns originating acts; bounded-autonomy concerns whose rule governs.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. The phrase is also used in sociology.

common_meaning: Self-rule within a scope whose limits are set by someone else.
example: The regional parliament has bounded-autonomy over schools and roads.
rrgm_bridge: Inside the scope the rule is the entity's own. Who sets the scope, and whether it can widen, are the questions that matter.
invariant_mi: Self-rule exercised within a scope whose limits are set from outside.

domain_entries.REL: Devolved government; professional discretion within protocols.
domain_entries.DIG: A system acting independently within limits set by its operators.

count_condition: An entity, a scope set from outside, and self-direction within it.
transfer_boundary: Not the illusion of autonomy. If the bounds can be changed at will with no recourse, the arrangement is also one of arbitrary-control.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: Choice among options that someone else has limited in advance.
example: A menu offers bounded-choice.
rrgm_bridge: Free selection inside a given set. Choosing within the set is not consenting to the set.
invariant_mi: Choice made among options that have been limited in advance.

domain_entries.REL: Constrained options, benign as in a menu or controlling as in a closed group.
domain_entries.ECO: Selection from a restricted choice set.
domain_entries.DIG: Selection from a fixed list of permitted outputs or actions.

count_condition: A chooser, a limited option set, and selection within it.
transfer_boundary: Benign when the limiting is open; controlling when it is hidden and alternatives are made unthinkable. Not bounded-rationality.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The idea that people make decisions with limited information, time, and thinking capacity, and so settle for good enough.
example: Bounded-rationality explains why shoppers stop at the first acceptable price.
rrgm_bridge: Reasoning on what is available. It applies to any finite reasoner.
invariant_mi: Rationality as exercised under limits of information, time, and computing capacity, aiming at good enough.

domain_entries.COG: Decision-making by satisficing and rules of thumb.
domain_entries.ECO: A revision of the fully rational agent of classical theory.
domain_entries.DIG: Agents optimising under limits of computation and context.

count_condition: A reasoner, identified limits, and decisions adequate within them.
transfer_boundary: Bounded rationality is not irrationality and not mere bias.
remainder_note: An established term from Herbert Simon. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A refusal limited to one stated matter, leaving the rest of the task or relationship in place.
example: "I won't sign that clause, but the rest is fine" is a bounded-refusal.
rrgm_bridge: Declines the specific thing, says so, and carries on with the rest.
invariant_mi: A refusal limited to a stated matter, which declines that matter and leaves the rest of the relation or task standing.

domain_entries.REL: Declining one request without ending the relationship.
domain_entries.DIG: Declining one part of a task and completing the remainder.

count_condition: A specific matter refused, a stated scope, and continued engagement otherwise.
transfer_boundary: Not withdrawal, a blanket refusal, or a block imposed from outside.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. An alternative reading is a power of refusal that is itself limited.

common_meaning: Risk whose worst possible outcome is limited in advance.
example: Buying the option gave him bounded-risk: he could lose the premium and no more.
rrgm_bridge: The bound is only as good as the mechanism that enforces it.
invariant_mi: Risk whose worst outcome is limited in advance to a known amount or scope.

domain_entries.ECO: Limited liability and capped-loss positions.
domain_entries.DIG: Sandboxed or staged changes that confine the damage of failure.

count_condition: A risk, a limiting mechanism, and a stated worst case.
transfer_boundary: Bounded is not small and not unlikely.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: Support given within stated limits of scope or time.
example: The mentoring scheme offers bounded-support: six sessions, then review.
rrgm_bridge: Helps without taking over and without running on indefinitely. The limits protect both sides.
invariant_mi: Support given within stated limits of scope or duration.

domain_entries.REL: Time-limited or role-limited assistance.
domain_entries.COG: Scaffolding that is withdrawn as the learner gains skill.
domain_entries.DIG: Assistance scoped to a task or role.

count_condition: A supporter, a recipient, and stated limits on the support.
transfer_boundary: Bounded support is not withheld support, and not support with strings attached.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The quality of having limits.
example: The proof depends on the boundedness of the sequence.
rrgm_bridge: Having an edge. In grammar, bounded things are counted and unbounded stuff is measured, which parallels the link between boundary and count.
invariant_mi: The property of having limits that are not exceeded.

domain_entries.FOR: Of a set, function, or sequence: contained within finite limits.
domain_entries.LIN: Of an event or entity: having a natural end point or edge, which underlies count nouns and completed events.
domain_entries.COG: Of a reasoner's resources: limited.
domain_entries.DIG: Of a queue, loop, or buffer: having a fixed maximum.

count_condition: A thing and limits it does not exceed.
transfer_boundary: Bounded is not finite: a bounded interval has infinitely many points. Not closed. The parallel with RRGM count is [HYP].

common_meaning: To bend the head or upper body as a sign of respect or greeting; to yield; the front of a ship.
example: The actors bowed to the audience.
rrgm_bridge: A lowering of oneself before another, made as a sign. To "bow out" is to withdraw with notice.
invariant_mi: To incline the head or body before another as a sign, or to give way.

domain_entries.REL: A gesture of respect, greeting, or submission; yielding to pressure or authority.
domain_entries.PHY: The forward end of a vessel.
domain_entries.LIN: Pronounced to rhyme with "cow"; a different word from s2.

count_condition: A party, another before whom it inclines or gives way, and the gesture or yielding.
transfer_boundary: Bowing to a decision is not agreeing with it. Bowing out is a declared withdrawal.

common_meaning: A weapon for shooting arrows; a knot with two loops; a rod strung with hair for playing a violin; a curve.
example: She tied the ribbon in a bow.
rrgm_bridge: A curve held under tension, storing what it will release.
invariant_mi: A curved piece held in tension, or a thing of that shape.

domain_entries.PHY: A sprung arc that stores energy and releases it into an arrow.
domain_entries.LIN: The stick drawn across strings to sustain a note; pronounced to rhyme with "low".
domain_entries.MYT: The weapon of divine archers; the rainbow as a sign in the sky.

count_condition: A curved form, usually under tension.
transfer_boundary: A separate word from s1.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: The curved shock wave that forms in front of an object moving faster than sound through a gas, or where a planet's magnetic field meets the solar wind.
example: The spacecraft crossed Earth's bow shock on its way out.
rrgm_bridge: The medium registers the body before reaching it: the disturbance stands off ahead of the boundary.
invariant_mi: A standing shock wave ahead of a body or field that a supersonic flow meets.

domain_entries.PHY: Found ahead of planets with magnetic fields and ahead of fast-moving stars.

count_condition: A supersonic flow, an obstacle, and an abrupt slowing and heating of the flow ahead of it.
transfer_boundary: The bow shock is not the boundary of the obstacle. Whether the Sun's own bubble has one is disputed. Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

common_meaning: A round, deep dish; a rounded hollow; to roll a ball.
example: She filled the bowl with soup.
rrgm_bridge: An open vessel: it receives, holds for a while, and can be poured from. Its emptiness is what makes it useful.
invariant_mi: An open rounded vessel, wider than deep, or a hollow of that shape.

domain_entries.PHY: A dish or natural hollow.
domain_entries.REL: The alms bowl of a mendicant; a stadium; the game of bowls.

count_condition: A rounded open container or hollow.
transfer_boundary: A bowl is not a plate, a cup, or a basin.

common_meaning: A container with a flat base and sides, usually with a lid; an enclosed or marked-off area; to fight with the fists.
example: The books arrived in a cardboard box.
rrgm_bridge: Fixes an inside and an outside by straight edges. That is convenient for handling and misleading when the thing put in it does not have that shape.
invariant_mi: A rigid container with flat sides, or an enclosed space marked off like one.

domain_entries.PHY: A rigid, usually rectangular container.
domain_entries.DIG: An on-screen area; a "sandbox" that confines a program; a "black box" known only by its behaviour.
domain_entries.REL: The sport of boxing; to "box in" is to leave someone few options.
domain_entries.LIN: A space on a form; "outside the box": beyond the usual assumptions.

count_condition: A rigid enclosure or a marked-off space with definite edges.
transfer_boundary: A black box is unopened, which is not the same as unknowable. Boxing is a separate word in origin.
remainder_note: Source IDs B030 and B231; both kept.

common_meaning: A male child or young man.
example: The boy ran to catch the bus.
rrgm_bridge: An age word for a person. Used of an adult it withholds adult standing.
invariant_mi: A male child, from birth to adulthood.

domain_entries.BIO: A juvenile human male.
domain_entries.REL: A social category with its own roles and rites; as a term for an adult man, historically a way of marking subordination.
domain_entries.PEJ: "Boy" addressed to a grown Black man: a racist form of address from slavery and segregation that denied his adulthood. Provisional domain.

count_condition: A young human male below the age taken as adulthood.
transfer_boundary: Where boyhood ends is set by culture and law. Calling an adult "boy" is demeaning.

common_meaning: A device that supports or holds something firmly; a pair; a curly bracket; to prepare for something difficult.
example: He wore a brace on his knee.
rrgm_bridge: Holds parts firm against a load, or makes oneself firm before one arrives.
invariant_mi: Something that holds parts firmly or supports against load; to make firm in readiness.

domain_entries.PHY: A structural member that stiffens a frame.
domain_entries.BIO: A device applied to the body to support a joint or move teeth.
domain_entries.FOR: The curly bracket, used to mark sets and blocks.
domain_entries.COG: To ready oneself for an expected shock.

count_condition: A load or expected load, and something made firm against it.
transfer_boundary: A brace supports; a splint immobilises. Curly braces, square brackets, and parentheses are different marks.
remainder_note: Source IDs B100 and B209; both kept.

common_meaning: A support fixed to a wall; either of a pair of marks used to enclose words or figures; a range or category.
example: The date is given in brackets.
rrgm_bridge: Sets something apart and holds it. RRGM practice keeps an empty bracket: a place held open for a claim that has not yet earned its entry.
invariant_mi: A pair of marks or a support that sets something apart and holds it; to set apart within such marks.

domain_entries.LIN: Punctuation enclosing an aside or insertion.
domain_entries.FOR: Marks that group terms and fix order of operation.
domain_entries.COG: To set a question aside without deciding it.
domain_entries.ECO: A range of income, age, or tax rate.
domain_entries.PHY: A projecting support; shots or exposures placed either side of a target to find it.
domain_entries.REL: The pairing chart of a tournament.

count_condition: Something set apart, and marks or a support that hold it apart.
transfer_boundary: Bracketing a question neither answers nor denies it. Moving into a higher tax bracket taxes only the excess.
remainder_note: Source IDs B180 and B208; both kept.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A slower than normal heart rate.
example: Trained athletes often have bradycardia at rest.
rrgm_bridge: A number below a conventional line. Whether it is a fault depends on whose heart it is and under what conditions.
invariant_mi: A heart rate below the conventional lower limit of normal.

domain_entries.BIO: Usually defined in adults as under sixty beats a minute; harmless in the fit and during sleep, serious when it starves the body of flow.

count_condition: A measured resting heart rate below the stated threshold.
transfer_boundary: Bradycardia is a finding and not a disease. The threshold is a convention.

common_meaning: The organ inside the head that controls thought, memory, feeling, and movement; intelligence.
example: The brain uses a fifth of the body's energy.
rrgm_bridge: The organ from which most words for minds were taken. The Coinage Protocol's map from it to digital structure is for locating invariants and asserts no likeness.
invariant_mi: The organ of the central nervous system that integrates sensing, control, and thought in animals that have one.

domain_entries.BIO: A mass of nerve tissue with tens of billions of neurons in humans.
domain_entries.COG: The organ whose activity is associated with mind; how the two relate is contested.
domain_entries.DIG: A loose inspiration for artificial neural networks; as "the brain of the system", a metaphor for the controlling part.
domain_entries.LIN: Figurative: intellect, or the person who does the thinking.

count_condition: An animal with a centralised nervous system and its principal organ.
transfer_boundary: Brain is not mind, and intelligence does not require one of the vertebrate kind. "Electronic brain" imports more than it shows.

common_meaning: A sudden clever idea; a group discussion to produce ideas; to produce ideas freely.
example: The team held a brainstorm on names for the product.
rrgm_bridge: A proposing mode. Everything it yields enters as a candidate, and nothing is promoted by having been said.
invariant_mi: To generate many ideas freely, with judgement postponed.

domain_entries.COG: Idea generation without immediate evaluation.
domain_entries.REL: A group method with a rule against criticism during generation.
domain_entries.DIG: Use of a generative system to produce candidate ideas.

count_condition: A question, many ideas produced, and evaluation deferred.
transfer_boundary: A brainstormed idea is not a decision or a plan. Groups do not reliably out-produce the same people working alone.

common_meaning: A part of a tree growing out from the trunk; a division of a river, family, organisation, or subject; to divide.
example: The bank closed its village branch.
rrgm_bridge: Diverges and stays joined. RRGM notes treat a role as a branch of one self, and ask whether the branch keeps the ability to judge the branch.
invariant_mi: A part that diverges from a main stem and continues as a line of its own, still joined to its source.

domain_entries.BIO: A limb of a tree; a division of a nerve, vessel, or lineage.
domain_entries.DIG: A parallel line of development in version control; a point where a program takes one of several paths.
domain_entries.REL: A local office; one of the divisions of government.
domain_entries.FOR: One of the values of a many-valued function; a path in a tree.

count_condition: A main stem, a point of divergence, and a continuing line from it.
transfer_boundary: A branch shares the history before the split. A fork is a separate copy with its own owner. Branches may or may not merge back.
remainder_note: Source IDs B091 and B232; both kept.

common_meaning: The rules that decide which path is taken at each choice point; the reasoning that applies within one path.
example: The survey's branch-logic skips the pet questions for people without pets.
rrgm_bridge: Reasoning inside a branch holds under that branch's assumption. Carrying it outside the branch is an import from the wrong stage.
invariant_mi: The rules that decide which branch is taken at each point of choice, or the reasoning that holds within one branch.

domain_entries.DIG: Conditional routing in programs, forms, and workflows.
domain_entries.FOR: Reasoning by cases, each under its own assumption.
domain_entries.COG: Reasoning local to a role or scenario.

count_condition: A point of choice, conditions, and the branches they select; or a branch and reasoning confined to it.
transfer_boundary: A conclusion reached within a branch is conditional on that branch. Not bridge-logic.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. Two readings are kept in one entry.

common_meaning: The point at which something divides into branches.
example: The trail's branch-point is marked by a cairn.
rrgm_bridge: Where alternatives part. Before it there is one line; after it, which line was taken is part of the record.
invariant_mi: The point at which one line divides into two or more.

domain_entries.BIO: A site where a vessel, pathway, or molecule divides.
domain_entries.FOR: A point around which a many-valued function passes from one value to another.
domain_entries.DIG: The commit or instruction at which paths diverge.
domain_entries.COG: A decision point from which outcomes diverge.

count_condition: A single line, a point, and two or more lines continuing from it.
transfer_boundary: Proposed distinctions: a branch-point is where paths divide; a break-point is where something gives way; a breakpoint is a chosen stop.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: Dividing into branches; a pattern of repeated division.
example: The branching of the river forms a delta.
rrgm_bridge: Division repeated until a tree forms. The number of branches at each step decides how fast the whole grows.
invariant_mi: The division of one line into several, repeated so as to form a tree.

domain_entries.BIO: The growth pattern of airways, vessels, nerve cells, and lineages.
domain_entries.FOR: A process in which each member produces a random number of successors; the share of decays going each way.
domain_entries.DIG: Creating development lines; the number of choices at each node of a search.
domain_entries.LIN: The direction in which a language builds its phrases.

count_condition: A line, repeated division, and a resulting tree.
transfer_boundary: A high branching factor makes exhaustive search impossible quickly.

common_meaning: Ready to face danger or pain; to face or endure.
example: It was brave of her to speak up.
rrgm_bridge: Fear is present and does not decide.
invariant_mi: Acting as one judges right in the face of danger, pain, or fear.

domain_entries.COG: Acting despite fear.
domain_entries.REL: Praised conduct in danger, including the risk of speaking against power.

count_condition: A danger or cost, awareness of it, and action taken regardless.
transfer_boundary: Brave is not fearless and not reckless. As praise it can patronise.

common_meaning: Courageous behaviour or character.
example: She received a medal for bravery.
rrgm_bridge: The quality as shown in deeds and recognised by others.
invariant_mi: The quality of acting rightly despite danger or fear.

domain_entries.COG: Physical, moral, and psychological courage.
domain_entries.REL: Conduct honoured by awards and remembered in a group's stories.

count_condition: Acts in the face of danger or cost, attributable to the agent.
transfer_boundary: Bravery is not bravado, which is a show of boldness.

common_meaning: A food made of flour, water, and usually yeast, mixed and baked; (informal) money.
example: The smell of fresh bread filled the kitchen.
rrgm_bridge: Sharing it is one of the oldest signs of fellowship: "companion" means one who shares bread.
invariant_mi: A staple food made by baking a dough of flour and water.

domain_entries.BIO: Dough raised by fermentation and set by baking.
domain_entries.ECO: A staple whose price is politically sensitive; a slang word for money or livelihood.
domain_entries.REL: The shared loaf as a sign of hospitality and fellowship.
domain_entries.MYT: Sacramental bread in several religions.
domain_entries.LIN: "Breadcrumbs": a trail left to find the way back.

count_condition: A baked dough of flour and water.
transfer_boundary: Bread may be leavened or not. The line between bread and cake is drawn differently by different tax codes.

common_meaning: The distance from side to side; wide range or extent.
example: The course is known for its breadth.
rrgm_bridge: Breadth and depth trade against each other under any fixed budget. Saying which one a piece of work chose is part of describing it.
invariant_mi: Extent from side to side, or the range of different things covered.

domain_entries.PHY: The dimension of width.
domain_entries.COG: The range of a person's knowledge or attention.
domain_entries.DIG: Breadth-first search explores all neighbours before going deeper.

count_condition: A thing and its extent across, or the range it covers.
transfer_boundary: Breadth is not depth and not thoroughness.

common_meaning: To separate into pieces by force; to stop working; to interrupt; to fail to keep; a pause.
example: The cup will break if you drop it.
rrgm_bridge: A break ends a continuity. Which continuity is the question: a structure can break while the identity it carried goes on, and the reverse.
invariant_mi: To end the continuity of something: by force, by pause, or by violation.

domain_entries.PHY: To fracture.
domain_entries.REL: To violate a rule, promise, or trust.
domain_entries.DIG: To exit a loop; to stop working; a "breaking change" makes dependent code fail.
domain_entries.COG: To decipher; to pause.
domain_entries.LIN: A division in a line or page.

count_condition: Something continuous and an event that ends its continuity.
transfer_boundary: To break is not to bend. A break taken as a pause intends resumption. Not every break is final.

common_meaning: To stop working; to collapse; to separate into parts; to overcome.
example: Enzymes break-down starch into sugars.
rrgm_bridge: The same words cover falling apart and taking apart on purpose. Analysis is the second, done so that the parts can be put back.
invariant_mi: To cease to hold together or function; or to take something apart into its components.

domain_entries.PHY: Of machinery or insulation: to fail.
domain_entries.BIO: To decompose a substance into simpler ones.
domain_entries.COG: To divide a task or problem into steps; to lose composure.
domain_entries.REL: Of talks or order: to fail; of barriers: to be overcome.

count_condition: A whole, and its failure to hold or its division into parts.
transfer_boundary: To break down keeps all the parts; to boil down discards the inessential ones.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. Verb form; the noun is entered at B194 breakdown.

common_meaning: The point at which something gives way under strain; in tennis, a point that could win the game against the server.
example: After a week without sleep he had reached his break-point.
